RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agree to the
Council engaging in consideration of the proposal for the rebuild
of the building with a revised footprint.
topline: The Council has decided to engage in consideration of a proposal for the rebuild of the Punch Bowl building with a revised footprint.

content:
Mr G Howard spoke
in opposition to the application.
 
Councillor S Farmer
was granted permission to speak and spoke in support of the
application.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
GRANT planning
permission subject to the following conditions (condition 4 being
the additional condition requested by committee):-
 
1.         Unless
explicitly required by condition within this consent, the
development hereby permitted shall be carried out in complete
accordance with the proposals as detailed on drawings:
 
           
Location Plan
           
Front Elevation
           
Left Elevation
           
Right Elevation
 
           
REASON:  For the avoidance of doubt and
to clarify which plans are relevant to the consent hereby
approved.
 
2.         The use
hereby approved shall only be operated between the following
hours:
 
           
9am – 8pm Monday to Friday
           
10am – 4pm Saturday
 
           
REASON: In the interests of residential amenity.
 
3.        
Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning
(Use Classes) Order 1987 (as amended) or any subsequent
re-enactment, the building hereby approved for the change of use
shall only be used for beauty and massage therapy (sui generis use
class) and for no other purpose.
 
           
REASON: To clarify the permitted use of the building to protect the
character and function of the immediate area.
 
4.         The use
hereby approved shall only be operated by the applicant ‘Mrs
D Beardmore’ residing at 8 Bank Cottages.  For the avoidance of doubt when the premises cease
to be occupied by the applicant, or when the applicant no longer
resides at 8 Bank Cottages, the use hereby permitted shall cease
and all materials and equipment brought on to the premises in
connection with the use shall be removed.
 
Reason: The use has
been permitted on the merits of this particular
application. Allowing the use to be operated by a different
business or by persons who do not occupy the associated residential
property would give rise to impacts that require further
consideration.
topline: The Planning and Development committee has decided to grant planning permission for a beauty and massage therapy business with specific conditions.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report seeking Committee approval to
undertake the statutory Scoping Consultation for the new Ribble
Valley Local Plan.
 
It was noted that
the consultation represents the first consultation stage in the new
plan-making process and will seek views from residents, businesses
and stakeholders on the issues, priorities and opportunities the
Local Plan should address, as well as how future engagement should
be undertaken. It will take place between 3 July and 14 August
2026.
 
The report also
sought approval of the supporting consultation materials, the
re-opening of the Call for Sites exercise, and the progression of
the remaining preparatory stages required to pass through Gateway
One.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    That this Committee
approve the Notice of Scoping Consultation (Appendix 2 of the
report) and make available in accordance with the regulation
requirements, and a 6 week
representation period is commenced during which representations on
the matters contained within it may be received by the Council.
 

2.    That this Committee
approve the Draft Local Plan Scoping Document (Appendix 3 of the
report) for public consultation alongside the formal Notice of
Scoping Consultation, for a 6 week
period commencing 03 July 2026.
 

3.    That, up to the start of
the consultation period, the Director of Economic Development and
Planning  be
authorised by this Committee to make minor changes to the wording
or layout of the Draft Local Plan Scoping Document (Appendix 3 of
the report) to improve clarity or accuracy of the document as
necessary and providing that the changes do not materially change
the meaning of the consultation document.

 

4.    That this Committee
approve the re-opening of the Call for Sites exercise for a period
of 6 weeks, running concurrently with the Scoping Consultation.
 

5.    That the Director of
Economic Development and Planning, in consultation with the
Committee Chair, and where appropriate, seeking the views of the
Local Plan Working Group be authorised by this Committee to
progress plan making through Gateway One by approving and
publishing the Gateway One Readiness Self-Assessment (Regulation
21); Summary of Consultation Responses; Updated Local Plan
Timetable; and Community Engagement Strategy.
topline: The Director of Economic Development and Planning has decided to approve the statutory Scoping Consultation for the new Ribble Valley Local Plan.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report
providing committee with information on forthcoming changes to the
provisions of declarations of interests.
 
In response to concerns about the safety of
Councillors, the Government had introduced section 65 of the
English Devolution and Community Empowerment Act 2026, which
amended the provisions of the Localism Act 2011 to include an
additional section 32A. This change provided that, where a
Councillor had declared a disclosable pecuniary interest in
relation to their usual residential address, the Council should not
include that information in the public register.
 
The Council’s Code of Conduct for
Members included a section on sensitive interests which had been
amended to make clear the new position and responsibilities with
regard to residential addresses. Those amendments were provided in
track changes for Member’s consideration.
 
At the meeting, members of the Committee spoke
in support of the changes and the additional safeguarding this
would provide.
 
***RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the amendments to the Code of Conduct
for Members in principle as shown in the appendix to the report and
referred it to the Council for adoption.
topline: The Accounts and Audit Committee has decided to approve amendments to the Code of Conduct for Members regarding the disclosure of residential addresses.

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report for Committee to consider the
Local Code of Corporate Governance for 2026/27.
 
The Code was reviewed and approved annually by
this committee and was the Council’s forward-looking
statement of how the governance culture of the organisation was
driven. Within the framework there were seven core principles that
looked to steer the application of good governance in everything
that members and staff undertook by highlighting how their work on
behalf of the council would be approached.
 
The document clearly communicated the key
Governance principles and the expected ‘behaviours’ or
culture that the CIPFA/Solace publication ‘Delivering Good
Governance in Local Government’ would expect. There was clear
linkage to how such ‘behaviours’ or culture could be
evidenced within the Council, principle by principle.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the reviewed Local Code of Corporate
Governance as attached to the report.
topline: The Accounts and Audit committee has decided to approve the Local Code of Corporate Governance for 2026/27.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report updating Committee on the Crisis and
Resilience Fund.
 
The scheme was launched as a ‘soft
launch’ with limited promotion to enable the housing team to
start implementing suitable processes and more importantly to bring
in the additional resource necessary to administer this scheme.
Consideration of suitable external resource in respect of the
resilience and community co-ordination arms of the funding had been
explored since the last Committee, and the report sought authority
to provide suitable resilience advice along with suggested
community funding. Details of the proposals along with draft
Service Level Agreements were provided to Member’s
consideration in regard to the following:
 

·      
Monetary advice provided by an extension to service already
provided by The Oaks Money Advice Centre at Trinity Community Hub
in Clitheroe.

·      
Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) Programmes, including a
‘Power Up’ Fitness Programme for young people aged
11-16 at both Roefield Leisure and Longridge Community Gym, and a
half-term extension programme providing support to local families
with the provision of healthy meals alongside engaging and
enriching activities.
 
Members supported the schemes and were keen to
ensure the services were available in both Clitheroe and
Longridge.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approve utilising £19,768 of the Councils’ CRF funding
to provide monetary advice resilience services in both Clitheroe
and Longridge.
 

2.    
Approved utilising £38,000 of the Councils’ CRF funding
to extend the Borough’s HAF offer for 2026/27 and delegated
responsibility to the Director of Economic Development and Planning
in consultation with the Chairman of Policy and Finance Committee
to negotiate terms in the event of any issues.
 

3.    
Approved the exemptions to the Council’s Contract Procedure
Rules as detailed within Section 4 of the report.
 
Councillor S Atkinson returned to the
meeting.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to allocate funds from the Crisis and Resilience Fund for monetary advice services and extend the Holiday Activities and Food Programmes in Clitheroe and Longridge.

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report informing members of the
Government’s consultation on the proposed High Value Council
Tax Surcharge and to seek approval from committee for the
Council’s response to the consultation.
 
The Government’s consultation proposed
the introduction of a High Value Council Tax Surcharge from April
2028 and sought the Councils views on a number of aspects of the
proposed scheme. The proposal would apply to residential properties
with a value of £2 million or more and would introduce
additional annual charges ranging from £2,500 to £7,500
depending on the property’s value.
 
Whilst the number of affected properties was
likely to be relatively small, the proposals may have
administrative and financial implications for billing authorities.
The consultation included consideration of the impacts on
vulnerable residents, including those who may be asset rich but
income poor.
 
The proposed response supported clear and
nationally consistent deferral arrangements to mitigate potential
adverse impacts. Members discussed the proposals and spoke both for
and against the introduction of the scheme, with the following
points of note:
 

·      
It was suggested that the surcharge be based on the equity in the
property not the total value

·      
The requirement for the Government to review the Council Tax system
as a whole

·      
Concerns in regard to enforcement, particularly where property
owners were based oversees and the cost benefit of enforcement in
those cases.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved the consultation response attached at Annex 1 subject to
minor amendments as discussed at the meeting.
 

2.    
Authorised the Acting Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive, in consultation with the Chairman of Policy and Finance
Committee, to make the minor amendments required before
submission.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the Council's response to the Government's consultation on the proposed High Value Council Tax Surcharge.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report
outlining the requirements to progress the development of the
Council’s contaminated land strategy and request approval for
a supplementary estimate of £30,000 to allow for specialist
consultancy input.
 
The Council first adopted a Contaminated Land
Inspection Strategy in 2001. This now required updating and
officers had commenced the work to do so. It was proposed that the
approval of the strategy and ongoing monitoring of progress would
be the responsibility of Community Services Committee.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Considered the issues raised in the report and
approved a supplementary estimate of £30,000 to allow for
specialist consultancy input, funded from the Insurance Earmarked
Reserve (£5,716) and the Pensions Triennial Revaluation
Reserve (£24,284).
 
Councillors L Jameson, R Ray and J Rogerson
left the meeting in respect of the next agenda item.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve a supplementary estimate of £30,000 for specialist consultancy input for the Council's contaminated land strategy.

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy Chief Executive
submitted a report for committee to consider and approve the
grant criteria and conditions for a new grant scheme to support
Town and Parish Councils with the cost of preparing Traffic
Management Plans for community events taking place during the
2026/27 financial year.
 
In March 2026, Committee resolved to set aside
£15,000 of the 2026/27 Voluntary Organisation Grant scheme
budget, to provide the grants of up to £1,000 per Parish or
Town Council. It was proposed that the scheme be trialled until the
end of the 2026/27 financial year and report would be brought back
to Committee following closure of the grant scheme to provide an
update to committee on the number of applications received and the
number and cost of grants awarded during the period.
 
Members spoke in support of the scheme. Whilst
the grants were limited to one application per Parish or Town
Council, Committee supported a suggestion to include a condition
that the grant could be used by the Parish/Town Council to support
more than one event.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved the grant scheme criteria and conditions as set out at
paragraph 3.1 with the condition that the grant may be used by the
receiving Parish/Town Council to support more than one event within
the Parish area.
 

2.    
Delegated the awarding of grants to officers administering the
scheme, provided that grant applications received are in line with
the final conditions and criteria approved by this Committee.
 

3.    
Approved that applications may be submitted retrospectively for
community events that incurred Traffic Management Plan costs
between 1 April 2026 and the date on which the approved scheme goes
live.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve a new grant scheme to support Town and Parish Councils with Traffic Management Plans for community events.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report updating Committee on the Ribble Valley
Shared Prosperity and Jubilee Fund and to seek approval for further
schemes.
 
The report provided a list of the approved
schemes totalling £876,228, which were progressing through
the grant agreement stage and completion.
 
Details of the full applications which had

consideration which totalled £197,715 along with details of
further schemes as recommended by the working group. At the
meeting, Members were asked to consider a further expression of
interest from Slaidburn Archive for £3066 which would be
invited to full application stage along with those listed.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Confirmed acceptance of the two full applications from Sabden
Parish Council and St Mary’s Centre Community Hall (at
section 4 of the report) subject to a grant agreement.
 

2.    
Noted the two schemes at full application stage, Whalley
Educational Foundation and Chipping and District Memorial Hall, for
which further information was awaited.
 

3.    
Agreed to inviting the projects listed at paragraph 5.1 of the
report to full application stage.
 

4.    
Agreed to utilising £70,000 of the fund to support the
Jubilee Trail.
 

5.    
Agreed to increase the grant for Sawley Village Hall by

6.    
Noted the schemes for which the Working Group requested further

Noted the schemes which the Working Group did not support detailed

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report
advising Committee of the process undertaken by HR and the Policy

The Sub-committee recommended that Lawson
Oddie be appointed to the position of Director of Resources

***RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Recommended to Council the appointment of
Lawson Oddie as Director of Resources.

content:

consider the appointment of members to working groups for 2026/27

Approved the continuance of the following working groups under the

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report for Committee to consider a
request from Health and Housing Committee to utilise receipts from
discounted sales of affordable housing (which were now unrestricted
usable Capital Receipts) to increase the budget for the Landlord
Tenant Grants capital scheme in 2026-27 by £200k.
 
Health and Housing Committee had approved the
recommendation at their meeting on 4 June 2026 which proposed the
additional budget be funded from unrestricted capital receipts
following the sale of properties, originally purchased with S106
monies, and resold at a discount as affordable housing.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the request from Health and Housing
Committee to increase the 2026-27 budget on the Landlord Tenant
Grants capital scheme by £200k to £284,590 using
unrestricted capital receipts generated from the sale of affordable
housing properties, which were initially funded by S106 monies.

request from Planning and Development Committee for a supplementary
estimate of £9,000 to allow an Assistant Planning Officer to

Institute (RTPI) Accredited Planning Degree.
 
Planning and Development Committee had

Approved the supplementary estimate request of

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report for Committee to consider a
request from Health and Housing Committee to increase the annual
grant to Homewise by £10,000 to £15,760 and to fund the
increase through a virement from the Voluntary Organisation Grant
budget.
 
Health and Housing Committee had approved the
recommendation at their meeting on 4 June 2026 with several reasons
for the increase including no increase in the grant given by the
Council for the past four years, and the grant not covering core
organisational costs resulting in the service being subsidised by
neighbouring local authorities, making the position inequitable and
no longer financially sustainable.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the request from Health and Housing
Committee to increase the 2026-27 Homewise Grant budget by
£10,000 to £15,760 to be funded by a virement from the
Voluntary Organisation Grants scheme.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to increase the annual grant to Homewise by £10,000, funding it through a virement from the Voluntary Organisation Grant budget.

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report informing Members of the final
capital outturn of the 2025/26 capital programme for this committee
and to seek Member approval for the slippage of some capital scheme
budgets from the 2025/26 financial year to the 2026/27 financial
year.
 
Actual expenditure on the Committee’s
capital programme was £364,353 which was 16.8% of the revised
estimate budget. Of the nine schemes in the Committee’s
revised capital programme four were fully completed in-year, and
five were ongoing, resulting in the requested slippage from the
2025/26 financial year into the 2026/27 financial year totalling
£1,756,430.
 
Actual expenditure on the UK Shared Prosperity
Fund capital schemes was £403,207, which was 63.1% of the
revised estimate budget. Of the fourteen UKSPF schemes in the
capital programme six were completed in-year. The remaining eight
schemes were not completed in-year, resulting in requested slippage
from the 2025/26 financial year into the 2026/27 financial year
totalling £235,287.
 
Actual expenditure on the Rural England
Prosperity Fund capital schemes was £77,405, which was 59.5%
of the revised estimate budget. Of the eight Rural England
Prosperity Fund schemes in the capital programme, two were
completed in-year. The remaining six schemes were not completed
in-year, resulting in requested slippage from the 2025/26 financial
year into the 2026/27 financial year totalling £52,675.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved slippage of £1,756,430 on the main Policy and
Finance Committee capital schemes listed at paragraph 3.5 of the
report.
 

2.    
Approved slippage of £235,287 on the UK Shared Prosperity
Fund capital schemes.
 

3.    
Approved slippage of £52,675 on the Rural England Prosperity
Fund capital schemes.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the slippage of capital scheme budgets for various funds from the 2025/26 financial year to the 2026/27 financial year.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report for
Committee to agree the adoption of the Returning Officer’s
Scale of Fees in connection with any Borough and Parish Council By
Elections that might arise in 2026/27.
 
The Returning Officer was held personally
responsible for the organisation and conduct of every election held
within the Borough.
 
For Local Elections the Council were required
to set the fees which the Returning Officer should not exceed. A
scale of fees for Lancashire was developed by a working group of
Elections Officers in 2007, which had been updated annually in line
with inflation, general staff pay awards and guidance from DLUHC.
Members were asked to consider the updated scale of fees as
detailed in the report.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agreed the Returning Officers’ Scale of
Fees for any Borough or Parish By Election in 2026/27 as set out in
Section 4 of the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to adopt the Returning Officer's Scale of Fees for Borough and Parish Council By Elections in 2026/27.

RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the
continuation of the Climate Emergency Working Group for 2026/27

Councillors R

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report informing and sharing with Committee the
2025/2026 Climate Change Annual report that includes an update on
the progress achieved with the 2025/26 climate change action
plan.
 
The Climate Change
Action Plan for 2025/26 was adopted by Committee on 20 November
2025 and set out initiatives that have a tangible impact upon
climate change and reducing carbon emissions.  The Climate
Emergency Working Group (CEWG) had considered the 2025/25 Annual
Report which provided an update on the progress of the action plan
for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.  The CEWG felt
that a great deal had been achieved and discussed suggestions for
actions to be included in the action plan for 2026/27. The Chairman
also supported that the report and the achievements made should be
published on the Climate Change pages of the Council website.
 
The Annual Report
and Action Plan 2025/26 Performance Monitoring Update were detailed
in the appendix and considered by Members. 
 
A number of key
achievements were highlighted, including a significant reduction in
carbon dioxide emissions from Council operations and substantial
investment through the Shared Prosperity Fund/Jubilee Fund.
 
In relation to the
performance update, Members noted that two of the objectives had
been assigned red ratings. The first concerned the introduction of
Council e-pool cars, which would require significant capital
investment. Further work is therefore needed to assess its
viability. The second related to lobbying Government for funding to
support decarbonisation and the expansion of local low-carbon heat
networks. Members were advised, however, that opportunities to
pursue this had not been available.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Note the content of
the 2025/2026 Annual Climate Change Report that includes an update
on the progress achieved with the 2025/26 climate change action
plan, and agree to publish the report on the Council website.
topline: The Director of Community Services has decided to approve the recommendations and publish the 2025/26 Climate Change Annual Report on the Council website.

content:
The Director of Resources submitted a
report presenting Committee with a draft lobbying letter to
the Rt Hon Rachel Reeves, Chancellor of the Exchequer with regard
to reviewing and reducing the rates of fuel duty and VAT, and to
raise this matter in Parliament advocating for urgent action to
make fuel more affordable for all.
 
Members considered
the draft letter appended to the report and agreed that the section
entitled Fuel Pressures on Households should be amended to
refer not only to households, but also to small businesses and
rural farms, as these are similarly affected.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the letter
at Appendix 1 of the report to use the Council's influence to lobby
Government on the issue of reviewing and reducing fuel duty and VAT
rates in the UK.
topline: The Council has decided to approve a lobbying letter to the Chancellor of the Exchequer to review and reduce fuel duty and VAT rates in the UK.

content:
The Director of
Economic Development and Planning submitted a report asking
Committee to consider a virement within the tourism service and
budget.
 
Members were
advised that the proposals sought to create capacity within the
tourism service to respond to a changing marketplace by increasing
the use of technology, delivering better value for money, targeting
services more effectively, expanding income-generating promotional
activity, and strengthening the Ribble Valley brand.
 
It was noted that
the existing budget structure was outdated, being largely focused
on traditional marketing, and that recent trends, including
increased online engagement and event-based activity, had driven
changes such as greater reliance on casual staff and partnership
income.
 
The report outlined
the need to enhance social media and website management, strengthen
the role and support of the Ribble Valley Tourism Association
(RVTA), and reduce reliance on print-based marketing, while also
highlighting concerns regarding the value for money of the
Council’s contribution to Marketing Lancashire. Members
further noted the importance of increasing capacity to support
partnerships, develop new promotional approaches, and safeguard and
promote the Ribble Valley brand in light of forthcoming local
government changes.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
1.         Approve
the proposed virement to create a temporary staffing budget.
 

2.         Confirm
acceptance of an annual contribution from Ribble Valley Tourism
Association for Ribble Valley to assist with the administration and
online presence of the RVTA.
 
3.         Agree to
terminate the membership of Marketing Lancashire.
topline: The Economic Development has decided to approve recommendations for virement within the tourism service and budget to strengthen the Ribble Valley brand.

content:
The Director of
Community Services submitted a report presenting the 2026/27
Climate Change Action Plan to Committee for approval and formal
adoption.
 
The Climate Change
Working Group had met on 26 March 2026 and considered and agreed a
draft Action Plan for 2026/27, taking into account the actions
arising from the Motion: Declaration of a Climate Emergency, for
submission to Committee. The Plan was appended to the report for
consideration.
 
Committee noted
that the objectives, goals and actions within the Plan had been
reviewed in light of the Motion, with the current position
highlighted in the document. It also noted that budget preparation
for 2026/27 was already underway, including approval of fees and
charges and consideration of service budgets by service
committees.
 
Subject to
Committee approval, the Action Plan would inform service committees
and Council, who would be responsible for implementation, having
regard to all relevant financial, legal and regulatory
considerations.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the 2026/27
Climate Change Action Plan at Appendix 1 of the report for formal
adoption.
topline: The UK council has decided to approve and formally adopt the 2026/27 Climate Change Action Plan.

content:
The Chief Executive
submitted a report seeking Committee’s approval to include
the report of the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Working
Group within the Lancashire-wide response to the Ministry of
Housing, Communities and Local Government’s (MHCLG) request
for views to inform the Structural Change Order (SCO).
 
Committee was
advised that MHCLG had written to the fifteen Lancashire local
authorities inviting their views to support the development of the
SCO.  MHCLG had requested feedback on
five key areas: the names of the proposed new unitary authorities,
councillor numbers, warding arrangements, joint committees and
implementation teams, and parish elections. A response was required
by 16 June 2026, with a later deadline of 17 August 2026 set
for warding arrangements.
 
It was further
reported that MHCLG would accept single, joint, or collective
submissions. The Lancashire authorities had agreed to submit a
combined response, identifying areas of both agreement and
divergence.
 
Committee noted
that the LGR Working Group had met on 2 June 2026 to consider
Ribble Valley’s proposed response.  At the meeting, Members had expressed support for
the following:
 

A new Council with
Joint Committee model.
In relation to
Joint Committees, representation should be based on parity between
constituent councils, irrespective of council status.
There should be no
prior specification of the Chair or Vice-Chair of the Joint
Committee.
Political balance
should not be a requirement of the Joint Committee.
Mark Wynn being
identified as lead for the Implementation Team and the Single
Responsible Officer (SRO) for LGR in Lancashire.
Subject to the
unitary model adopted, the most experienced Returning Officer
within the area should be appointed – the names of the
proposed officers were provided in the report.
The Structural
Changes Order aligning future parish council elections with those
of the new authority (noting this is already the current position
for Ribble Valley Borough Council).
Further
discussions regarding a name for RVBC’s preferred new
authority model would follow once the Government have announced
their ‘minded to’ decision on which proposal to take
forward.
Under a
two-unitary authority (2UA) model, the allocation of 10 councillors
in total; and in all other models, 14 councillors.
Lancashire will
submit ward proposals as per the later deadline given by MHCLG of
17 August 2026.

 
Committee discussed
and agreed with the working group’s report and
recommendations.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the content
of the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Working Group report
be included in the Lancashire wider (L15) return to MHCLG as the
official Ribble Valley Borough Council (RVBC) response.
topline: The Chief Executive has decided to include the Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) Working Group report in the Lancashire-wide response to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government's request for views on the Structural Change Order (SCO).

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report seeking
Committee’s views on the need for working groups under the
remit of the Licensing committee.
 
At present, there were no active working
groups under the remit of the Licensing committee and Committee
confirmed if it was content to continue without any working
groups.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved that there was currently no need for
a working group under the remit of the Licensing committee.
topline: The Licensing committee has decided that there is currently no need for a working group under its remit.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report seeking
Committee’s views on whether the Council’s policy in
relation to hackney carriage and private hire licensing should be
reviewed to permit additional hackney carriage licenses being
issued where the vehicle was fully wheelchair
accessible.
 
Under the existing policy, the Council limited
the number of licenced hackney carriage vehicles to fifty-three and
all fifty-three hackney carriage plates had been issued. Of those
vehicles, four were fully wheelchair accessible and eight fitted
with Elap seats. The Council had received a request to consider
whether an additional hackney carriage plate could be issued for a
fully wheelchair accessible vehicle.
 
The report asked Members to consider whether to retain the
current policy, or to amend the policy to permit the additional
hackney carriage licenses under one of the following
approaches:
 

·      
Issuing a small number of additional hackney carriage plates solely
for wheelchair accessible vehicles

·      
Allowing the Council discretion to exceed the current limit where a
vehicle demonstrably improves accessibility provision

·      
Increasing the limit from 53 to a higher number, with a requirement
that any additional plates must be wheelchair accessible
 
Members supported the proposal and agreed that the demand
outweighed the provision of accessible vehicles. Members also noted
contributing factors including Ribble Valley issued hackney
carriages operating outside the Borough and guide dogs not being
permitted in some vehicles. The Council had a waiting list for
hackney carriage plates, and it was confirmed that the plates were
required to be returned to the Council when no longer required so
the Council could re-issue in accordance with the waiting
list.
 
A six-week public consultation would be
undertaken, with the results reported back to Committee on 8
September 2026 before any final decision was made.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Agreed in principle to review the current limit on hackney carriage
plates along with allowing the Council discretion to exceed the
current limit where a vehicle demonstrably improves accessibility
provision.
 

2.    
Authorised the Head of Legal and Democratic Services to undertake
consultation with licence holders and any other appropriate
consultees on any proposed amendment.
topline: The Licensing Committee has decided to review the policy on hackney carriage licensing to allow for additional licenses for fully wheelchair accessible vehicles.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report informing and
seeking Committee’s approval of a proposed response to
draft SIA section 12 statutory operational guidance published in
respect of Martyn’s Law.
 
The Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act
2025, often referred to as Martyn’s Law, received Royal
Assent on 3 April 2025, with a minimum implementation period of 2
years to allow venues sufficient time to understand and comply with
the new requirements. The report set out the responsibilities for
venues and event organisers which were being introduced. The Act
also required the production of two separate pieces of statutory
guidance, namely:
 

·      
Guidance from the Home Office for the public to understand how they
might meet the requirements of the legislation, which was appended
to the report.
 

·      
Guidance from the SIA which set out how the SIA will exercise its
regulatory powers, including its investigatory powers, as the
regulator for Martyn’s Law.
 
The report provided Committee with the SIA
guidance, which had now been issued, along with a consultation on
its content which was open until 12 June 2026. Members were asked
to consider the Council’s responses to the consultation, as
proposed in the report.
 
At the meeting, Members supported the
responses and welcomed both sets of guidance along with the
implementation of the legislation.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the proposed response to the
consultation and authorised the Head of Legal and Democratic
Services to submit it on behalf of the Council.
topline: The Licensing Committee has decided to approve a proposed response to draft SIA section 12 statutory operational guidance in respect of Martyn's Law.

content:
The Director of
Resources submitted a report reviewing the final outturn of the
2025/26 capital programme for this Committee and seeking Member
approval for the slippage of some capital scheme budgets from the
2025/26 financial year to the 2026/27 financial year.
 
The Committee
originally approved five capital schemes totalling
£3,160,390, including four new schemes for 2025/26 and three
carried forward from 2024/25. A further £755,680 of unspent
budget from six schemes was carried forward as slippage, alongside
an additional £139,384 for Disabled Facilities Grants funded
by external grants, and a reallocation of budgets within affordable
housing schemes. As a result, the total approved 2025/26 capital
programme was £4,055,454 across eleven schemes, which was
later revised to £2,871,540 after £1,099,620 was moved
into 2026/27 following a progress review/
 
It was noted that
actual expenditure on this Committee’s capital programme was
£2,223,674 which is 77.4% of the revised estimate budget. Of
the eleven schemes in the revised capital programme, two were
completed in-year. The remaining nine schemes were not completed
in-year resulting in slippage from the 2025/26 financial year into
the 2026/27 financial year totalling £815,630.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the
slippage of £815,630 as set out at paragraph 3.6 of the
report.
topline: The Health and Housing Committee has decided to approve the slippage of capital scheme budgets from the 2025/26 financial year to the 2026/27 financial year.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report updating
Committee in respect of the refurbishment works at the
Council’s temporary accommodation at the Joiners
Arms.
 
Members were advised the Architects had undertaken initial site
work and produced three layout options for the refurbishment, which
were detailed in the report.  However,
the estimated costs significantly exceed the approved
budget.
 
Committee further noted that, given the high refurbishment costs
and the age and condition of the building, an alternative option
had been explored involving the provision of new temporary
accommodation.  Officers reported that
there was the potential to purchase and redevelop a nearby
property.  Members were informed that
this option would require borrowing, potential grant funding and a
reappraisal of the capital programme. 
 
Following discussion, Committee indicated its in-principle
support for the use of the capital budget to provide alternative
temporary accommodation rather than refurbishing the Joiners Arms.
However, concerns were raised regarding the property identified by
officers, and it was agreed that further work should be undertaken
in relation to this and potentially other suitable
sites.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Approve
in principle the use of the capital budget to provide alternative
temporary accommodation.

 

2.        
Authorise the Director of Economic Development and Planning to
further explore the provision of bespoke temporary accommodation on
suitable sites and report back to Committee.
topline: The Committee has decided to explore alternative options for temporary accommodation rather than refurbishing the Joiners Arms.

content:

The report further
requested approval for an exemption from the Council’s

RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve an
exemption from the council’s Contract Procedure Rules (in

content:
This item was considered last on the
agenda.
 
Councillor M Hindle
left the meeting and took no part in the debate or the vote. As the
Vice Chair was not present, after a vote was taken, Councillor R
Elms acted as Chair for this item.
 
The Director of
Economic Development and Planning submitted a report seeking
approval for the annual grant payment to Homewise in support of the
provision of the Home Improvement Service within the borough.
 
Committee was
advised that Homewise had requested an annual uplift to the
existing Council grant in order to support the continued delivery
and long-term sustainability of services for vulnerable residents.
It was noted that the grant currently supported both the
Handyperson and Homecare Services, which required significant
investment and had been subject to rising costs in recent years,
whilst funding had remained unchanged. Members were informed that
the proposed uplift would increase service capacity, contribute
towards core costs, improve long-term sustainability, strengthen
community engagement, and help to ensure continued value for
money.
 
It was further
noted that Homewise currently undertook Memory Matters assessments
and administered dementia grants on behalf of the Council, and had
also requested an increase in the fees associated with this
work.
 
Following
discussion, Members agreed that the annual grant should be
increased in respect of the Handyperson and Homecare Services, but
that the Memory Matters assessments and administration of dementia
grants should be brought in-house. It was noted that the Council
could utilise the services of a qualified Occupational Therapist to
undertake the Memory Matters assessments in person for the purposes
of dementia grant applications.
 
Members also noted
that there would be resource implications for the Council’s
Housing department, and that these would need to be assessed and
kept under review.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.   Approve an increase in the
annual grant to Homewise to £15,760 and refer the matter to
Policy & Finance Committee to seek approval for a virement from
the Voluntary Organisation Grant budget to fund this increase.

 

2.   Approve that the Memory
Matters assessments and the administration of dementia grants be
brought in-house.
topline: The Council has decided to increase the annual grant to Homewise for Home Improvement Service and bring Memory Matters assessments and dementia grant administration in-house.

content:
The Director of Economic Development
submitted a report updating Committee on the Clitheroe
Market Improvements and seeking approval of an exemption to the
Council’s Contract Procedure Rules.
 
Committee were
advised that four companies were approached to quote for
undertaking a more detailed assessment of the interventions
required to secure safe routes into Clitheroe to improve the
non-car accessibility of the town. On the basis that only one quote
was received, an exemption in accordance with the Council’s
Contract Procedure Rules (CPR5) was requested from Committee.
 
Councillors D
Birtwhistle, M Sutcliffe and M Graveston were granted permission to
speak. Councillor Sutcliffe expressed support for active travel and
referred to related issues, including parking and opportunities to
enhance the attractiveness of Clitheroe town centre. Councillor
Graveston endorsed Councillor Sutcliffe’s remarks,
highlighted the importance of signage, and suggested that
consultants be engaged to consider wider improvements to the
market. Councillor Birtwhistle raised concerns about the use of
market funding for broader transport-related work.
 
Members discussed
the points raised, acknowledging that improvements to active travel
and accessibility could have a positive impact on both the market
and the town centre, whilst also recognising ongoing issues
relating to traffic, parking and signage. In relation to market
improvements more generally, Members noted the differing views of
traders and the need for clear direction, whilst also suggesting
practical improvements and continued collaboration through the
working group.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Approve
an exemption to the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules as
detailed within section 3 of the report.

 

2.         Approve
works being undertaken to replace the railings on the steps
adjacent to the market car park, at a cost of £3460.
topline: The Council has decided to approve an exemption to the Contract Procedure Rules for Clitheroe Market Improvements.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report
asking Committee to review and agree the new policy on ‘Civil
Penalties Under the Renters Rights Act 2025 and Other Housing
Legislation’.
 
The Committee was
reminded that the Renters’ Rights Act 2025 came into force on
1 May 2026, granting local authorities powers to issue civil
penalties to landlords and letting agents for a wide range of
housing offences.
 
Members noted that,
to promote consistency, the Association of Chief Environmental
Health Officers (ACEHO) had developed a template policy, and that
several North West authorities intended to adopt it.
 
The Head of
Environmental Health confirmed that the ACEHO policy had been
adopted as the basis for this Council’s approach.  Members considered the proposed policy, which
detailed the process for imposing civil penalties, the factors to
be considered when determining penalty levels, and the types of
offences to which penalties may apply.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.   Approve the proposed policy ‘Civil
Penalties Under the Renters Rights Act 2025 and Other Housing
Legislation’.
 

2.   Permit the Head of Environmental Health to
make amendments to the policy as necessary, without the need for
Committee approval.
topline: The Committee has decided to approve a new policy on civil penalties under the Renters Rights Act 2025 and other housing legislation.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report asking Committee to consider a
request to approve a Disabled Facilities Grant above the grant
maximum and to consider a request for approval of a procedure for
future applications.
 
It was noted that
rising building and labour costs were likely to increase the number
of Disabled Facilities Grant cases exceeding the maximum limit,
requiring more frequent exceptions. However given the limited
number of requests each year, rather than increasing the grant
maximum, it was proposed to delegate authority for approving
exceptions to the Director of Economic Development and Planning,
with regular updates being brought to the Committee.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
 

1.         Approve
an exception to the current Disabled Facilities Grant policy and
award a grant of a sum not exceeding £94,911.04.
 

2.         Approve
an amendment to the DFG policy so that such decisions will be
delegated to the Director of Economic Development and Planning.

content:
The Acting Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report to request that Committee

The introduction of formalised opening and closing arrangements at

·      
Arrangements for an existing member of staff to cover part of the

Approved the formalised opening and closing arrangements at the

Approved the proposed honoraria payment to the Refuse Collection

Approved the proposed payment of a market supplement to post M107

topline: The Personnel has decided to approve recruitment activity and proposed payments in Waste Services to ensure continuity of service.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report seeking
approval from Committee to update the Council’s Flexible
Working policy to reflect new proposed arrangements.
 
Office-based council employees were required
to work 7.24 hours per day, within a bandwidth period of 8am and
6pm. This was not as flexible as neighbouring authorities, and it
was proposed to extend these hours from 7.30am to 7pm.
 
Updated rules for working from home were also proposed,
reflecting that this had become the norm for many employees across
the country and in neighbouring authorities. The updated Flexible
Working Policy proposed that employees working from home would be
allowed to record the time they actually worked, rather than be
credited a standard working day.
 
The changes also included the replacement of the current
manual card system with a process of employees directly entering
their own time recording and adjustments on the system, without
further authorisation, reducing the resource requirement from PAs
and managers. It was confirmed at the meeting that managers would
be responsible for monitoring output and outcomes and managing any
issues.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved the working day bandwidth hours within the flexible
working policy being extended from 8am to 6pm to 7.30am to
7.00pm.
 

2.    
Approved the proposed amended Flexible Working Scheme as set out in
Appendix 1 to the report.
topline: The Personnel has decided to update the Council's Flexible Working policy to extend working hours and allow employees to work from home more flexibly.

topline: The Personnel has decided to approve training for an Assistant Planning Officer to complete a part-time post-graduate Royal Town Planning Institute Accredited Planning Degree.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report requesting
Committee authorisation that a market supplement be applied to the
role of Building Control Senior Surveyor.
 
The Council’s approach to the
application of market supplements was outlined in appendix 3 of the
Pay Policy statement which was included with the report. The key
points included:
 

·      
A market supplement
would be considered if retention problems were beingencountered
either for a job family or an individual post.

·      
The market supplement
would not exceed 4 increments.
 
It was considered that retention of the current postholder
was at serious risk as well as difficulties nationally in the
recruitment and retention in Building Control teams.
 
A review of the person specification and job
description for the role had not uncovered anything that needed
updating, therefore, there was no justification in undertaking job
evaluation.
 
It was proposed to apply a market supplement
of four increments, currently £4,127 per annum, to increase
the postholder’s current salary from PO5 (scp 35)
£46,142 to PO9 (scp 39) £50,269 per annum.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agreed to the application of a market
supplement payment of 4 increments (£4,127 per annum based on
current pay scales) to post D45 Senior Building Control Surveyor,
as outlined in the report.
topline: The Personnel has decided to approve a market supplement payment for the role of Building Control Senior Surveyor.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a report seeking
Committee’s approval of amendments to the Officer Code of
Conduct principle and its referral to Council.
 
The Code had been comprehensively reviewed and
required amendments had been made, namely:
 

·      
Paragraphs 13.1 to 13.5 set out the new provisions relating to
Gifts and Hospitality, how these should be recorded, financial
limits and the acceptance of Gifts and Hospitality.
 

·      
Paragraph 9 had been amended to include reference to the
Council’s duties pursuant to the Equality Act 2010 and its
public sector equality duty under Section 149 of the Equality Act.
It also included requirements relating to reasonable adjustments
and provides a link to the reasonable adjustments policy.
 

·      
Paragraph 3.3 had been added so that there was a direct link
between the code and the Local Code of Corporate Governance.
 
Following approval, the Constitution would be
updated to include the revised Code. 
The Staff Handbook would also be updated along with a roll out to
all staff.
 
***RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved in principle the revised Code of
Conduct for Officers as set out in Appendix 2 to the report and
recommended its adoption to Council.
topline: The Personnel has decided to approve recommendations for amendments to the Officer Code of Conduct principle.

content:

content:
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
GRANT planning
permission subject to the following conditions:-
 
1.         The
development must be begun not later than the expiration of three
years beginning with the date of this permission.
 
           
REASON: Required to be imposed by Section 51 of the Planning and
Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
 
2.         The
development hereby permitted shall not be carried out otherwise
than in conformity with the following submitted plans and details
and recommendations therein received by the Local Planning
Authority unless prohibited by any other condition.
 
Plans
 
Amended Location
Plan scale 1:1250 received 20 April 2026
Amended Proposed
Site Plan scale 1:500 received 19 May 2026
Proposed Elevations
drawing ref: 1271493 Ribble Valley BC
Amended Proposed
Equipment Details scale 1:150 received 19 May 2026
 
Documents
 
Amended Penine
Ecology Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment May 2026
Materials Schedule
received 19 May 2026
 
           
REASON: For the avoidance of doubt and to clarify which plans are
relevant to the consent.
 
3.         The
development shall be implemented in accordance with the hard
surfacing details provided within the document named ‘Ribble
Valley Borough Council – Materials Schedule’ received
19 May 2026.
 
REASON: To ensure
the proposal is satisfactorily landscaped and trees/hedgerow of
landscape/visual amenity value are retained as part of the
development.
 
4.         Prior to
the commencement of development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be
submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning
Authority (see further details below at 5 of the Notes Section) and
implemented in accordance with the approved details. The
Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be prepared in accordance with the
submitted Amended Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment by Pennine
Ecological dated May 2026.
 
REASON: To ensure
the development delivers a net gain off site which satisfies
paragraph 14 (2) of Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning
Act 1990 and which is in accordance with the biodiversity
information submitted with the planning application.
 
5.         Prior to
commencement of any site works including delivery of building
materials and excavations for foundations or services, all trees
within influencing distance of the proposed destination play area
shall be protected in accordance with BS5837 2012 [Trees in
Relation to Demolition, Design & Construction]  this includes all trees within influencing
distance of the foot print of any proposed equipment and access
paths specifically the  two mature
sycamore and four cherry trees growing within influencing distance
to the proposed access proposed path running on a north /south west
trajectory from the proposed access point from Edisford road. The
RPA [root protection area] shall be a minimum of a 12m RPA measured
from centre of the main stem of any said tree in accordance with
BS5837.
 
The tree protection
details shall be submitted to and inspected and agreed in writing
by the Council's Countryside Officer prior to any site works
commencing, along with a tree protection monitoring schedule.
 
The root
protection/exclusion zone shall remain in place until all building
work has been completed and all excess materials have been removed
from site including soil/spoil and rubble. During the building
works no excavations or changes in ground levels shall take place
and no building materials/spoil/soil/rubble shall be stored or
redistributed within the protection/exclusion zone, in addition no
impermeable surfacing shall be constructed within the protection
zone.
 
For the avoidance
of doubt no tree felling or pruning works are authorised as part of
the granting of this planning permission.
 
REASON: In order to
ensure that nearby trees of amenity value are afforded appropriate
protection from the potential adverse effects of development.
 
6.         For the
full period of construction, facilities shall be available on site
for the cleaning of the wheels of vehicles leaving the site and
such equipment shall be used as necessary to prevent mud and stones
being carried onto the highway. The roads adjacent to the site
shall be mechanically swept as required during the full
construction period. 
 
REASON: To prevent
stones and mud being carried onto the public highway to the
detriment of road
safety.
 
7.         No
external lighting/floodlighting or building mounted lighting shall
be erected or placed anywhere within the site to which this consent
relates without express planning permission first being
obtained.
 
REASON: To enable
the Local Planning Authority to exercise control over development
which could prove materially harmful the character and visual
amenities of the immediate area or wildlife.
 
Informative Note
5
 
The effect of
paragraph 13 of Schedule 7A to the Town and Country Planning Act
1990 is that planning permission granted for the development of
land in England is deemed to have been granted subject to the
condition "(the biodiversity gain condition") that development may
not begin unless:
 
(a) a Biodiversity
Gain Plan has been submitted to the local planning authority,
and
(b) the planning
authority has approved the plan.
 
Based on the
information available this permission is considered to be one which
will require the approval of a biodiversity gain plan before
development is begun because none of the statutory exemptions or
transitional arrangements listed in the legislation are considered
to apply.
 
The biodiversity
gain plan must include:
 
(a)        information about
the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of
the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any
other habitat;
(b)        the pre-development
biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;
(c)        the post-development
biodiversity value of the onsite habitat;
(d)        any registered
offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the
biodiversity and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to
the development;
(e)        any biodiversity
credits purchased for the development; and
(f)         such other
matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.
 
When calculating
the post-development biodiversity value of a habitat, the planning
authority can only take into account an increase in biodiversity
value post-development where it is satisfied that the habitat
creation or enhancements delivering the increase will be maintained
for at least 30 years after the development is completed.
topline: The Planning and Development Committee has decided to grant planning permission for a development project with stringent conditions related to biodiversity, tree protection, and road safety.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report seeking approval for amendments
to the Council’s scheme of delegation in respect of planning
matters, Planning and Development Committee terms of reference and
appointment of Nominated Officers and Nominated Members
 
The need for the
changes arose from the Government’s proposed Town and Country
Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions)
(England) Regulations 2026, which are expected to come into force
on 30 September 2026 following consultation earlier in the year.
The report outlined that the Council was required to update its
constitutional arrangements in advance, including revising the
scheme of delegation, amending committee terms of reference and
reducing committee membership. Members were advised of the proposed
amendments for in-principle approval by Committee and thereafter by
Full Council ahead of implementation, together with recommendations
to appoint the key nominated roles required under the new
framework.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Approve
(to take effect from the date that the 2026 Functions Regulations
come into force) the revised Scheme of Delegation in principle for
approval by Council.
 

2.         Approve
the Terms of Reference in principle (to take effect from the date
the 2026 Functions Regulations come into force) for approval by
Full Council
 
For
the purposes of the 2026 Functions Regulations appoint:
 

·        
the Chair of Planning and Development Committee as the Nominated
Member;

·        
the Vice Chair of Planning and Development Committee as the
Substitute Nominated Member.

content:
The Director of
Economic Development and Planning submitted a report seeking
confirmation as to whether Committee wished to respond to a
statutory consultation on the draft Regulations and guidance
underpinning the Government’s planning committee reforms
arising from the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025.
 
Members were
reminded that, in 2025, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and
Local Government (MHCLG) had published a paper on modernising
planning committees. The proposals included the introduction of a
national scheme of delegation, the creation of smaller, targeted
planning committees for strategic development, and a mandatory
training requirement for planning committee members. It was noted
that the Council had responded to this paper in January 2025.
 
On 26 March 2026,
MHCLG published a statutory consultation entitled Planning
committee reform: statutory consultation on draft Regulations and
guidance. Members noted that the Government proposed to bring
forward the Regulations and statutory guidance relating to the
national scheme of delegation and the size of planning committees,
with the intention that the reforms would be implemented by the end
of September 2026. The report set out details of the draft
Regulations and draft guidance.
 
It was further
noted that, on the same date, a new statutory instrument was
introduced requiring local planning authorities to notify the
Secretary of State where they intended to refuse planning
applications for 150 dwellings or more.
 
The consultation
sought views on the draft Regulations, the proposed approach to
phased reserved matters applications, and the draft statutory
guidance.
 
Members discussed
the proposals in detail and expressed strong concern about the
reforms. The majority of Members
considered that the proposals would undermine local democratic
accountability by significantly reducing the role of elected
members in planning decisions, limiting opportunities for debate,
and weakening residents’ ability to engage with the planning
process. Particular concern was raised
that increased delegation would restrict the ability to bring
contentious or locally sensitive applications before Committee.
 
Members also
highlighted the potential negative impact on public confidence in
the planning system, the relationship between councillors,
officers, and residents, and the additional pressure that could be
placed on planning officers. While it was acknowledged that the
reforms appeared to be aimed at authorities with high levels of
call?ins, Members considered that the Council’s existing
arrangements operated effectively and without undue delay.
 
There was broad
agreement that the Council should submit a clear and strong
objection to the consultation, reflecting opposition to the
principles underpinning the draft Regulations and guidance.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Note the changes
proposed and approve the submission of responses to consultation
questions one and three by the Director of Economic Development and
Planning, following consultation with the Chairman.
topline: The Council has decided to strongly object to proposed planning committee reforms, citing concerns about undermining local democratic accountability and limiting opportunities for debate.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report advising Members of the
proposed LGR Implementation Reserve Assurance Framework and seeking
approval to the signing of the Assurance Framework on behalf of
this Council.
 
The Committee noted
that the Lancashire Strategic LGR Chief Executives Board had
recommended establishing a single LGR Implementation Reserve to be
collectively managed with Lancashire County Council acting as host
authority.  The purpose of the Reserve would be to provide
sufficient programme capacity to ensure that the new unitary
authorities could deliver safe and legal services from 1 April
2028.
 
It was further
reported that the Lancashire Chief Financial Officers group would
formally establish as a Board to oversee the finance workstream,
and that Section 151 officers from all fifteen participating
councils would be required to approve the Assurance Framework.
 
Members were
advised that the £30m Reserve would fund eligible transition
costs, including staffing, consultancy, ICT, elections, shadow
council arrangements, legal advice and other essential expenditure.
Contributions were confirmed for all fifteen councils, with Ribble
Valley’s contribution of £487,571 already approved as
part of the 2026/27 budget. The value of the Reserve would be
reviewed as at 30 September 2026 and each council’s
contribution would remain conditional on all others making their
agreed payment.
 
It was reported
that the Reserve would be held by Lancashire County Council and
further operational details were included in the Annex to the
report. Committee noted that the Lancashire Chief Financial
Officers had reviewed and approved the Assurance Framework on 20
March 2026 subject to minor amendments, and that final agreement
would also be sought from the Lancashire Chief Executives
Group.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the signing
off of the Assurance Framework for the LGR Implementation
Reserve.

content:
At this point in
the meeting, the order of business was varied and Committee
proceeded to consider Item 18 next as it was a decision item.
 
The Chief Executive submitted a
report updating Committee on Local Government Reorganisation
(LGR), particularly ongoing capacity issues and workstream
leads.
 
Committee noted
that the Government had invited proposals for local government
reorganisation across all 21 county areas, and that five proposals
for Lancashire had been submitted by November 2025. The statutory
consultation had concluded on 26 March 2026, with a decision on the
new unitary footprints expected in summer 2026. It was reported
that a structural change order was anticipated in autumn 2026,
followed by the creation of shadow authorities and elections in May
2027, with existing councils ceasing on 1 April 2028.
 
Committee
recognised that all Lancashire Councils were required to cooperate
in preparing for reorganisation and that it was essential for
Ribble Valley to build organisational capacity to support a safe
and legal transition. Members were informed of the roles identified
to support this work, including a Programme Manager, Programme
Administrator, Finance Lead and Graduate Trainee, and noted the
estimated costs for these fixed?term posts. It was also reported
that some of these costs might be funded through the central
Implementation Reserve.
 
Committee
considered the proposed funding approach, which included increasing
the staff turnover allowance, using savings from delayed food?waste
collections, reallocating underspends from the Ribblesdale Pool
solar project, and drawing on surplus pay award contingency.
Members were reminded of the significant budget gaps forecast for
2027/28 and 2028/29 and the need for future savings.
 
Committee also
noted Lancashire?wide arrangements, including the establishment of
a programme team, consultancy support, data?sharing requirements
and the Council’s £487,000 contribution to the
transition fund.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Note the latest
position on Local Government Reorganisation in Lancashire.
 

2.         Approve the
funding proposals set out in section 3.8 of the report.
topline: The Committee has decided to approve funding proposals for Local Government Reorganisation in Lancashire.

The Director of
Economic Development and Planning submitted a report
updating Committee on the Crisis and Resilience Fund.

 
Committee noted
that the Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) had been introduced to
support low?income households facing financial shocks and to
strengthen long?term financial resilience, with funding available
from April 2026 to March 2029. Members were advised that the Fund
included a new Housing Payment element replacing Discretionary
Housing Payments and that authorities had discretion in how the
Fund was allocated within the Government’s framework.
Committee also noted the Fund’s key objectives, including the
delivery of effective crisis support, improving financial
resilience, and strengthening the local support landscape.

 
It was reported
that Lancashire County Council would receive £17.239m in
2026/27, with Ribble Valley’s share confirmed at
£408,750, including £37,251 for affordable warmth.
Further information was provided regarding County?level proposals,
including continuation of district?delivered cash?first schemes and
the expansion of resilience?based support. Members were informed
that an additional £97,266 had been allocated to Ribble
Valley to support low?income households reliant on heating oil.

 
Committee was
informed that Crisis Payments would operate year?round on a
needs?based, person?centred basis, with applications accepted
through multiple routes and decisions made within 48 hours wherever
possible. Housing Payments would closely replicate existing DHP
arrangements during a phased transition and would provide further
financial assistance towards housing costs. Members also noted that
authorities were required to develop Resilience Services and
community?coordination activity to build financial capability and
reduce repeat crises.

 
Committee
considered the proposed local approach, which included the
establishment of online and telephone application routes, direct
referral arrangements with key partners, and the creation of a
three?year Crisis and Resilience Officer post to administer the
scheme. Plans to provide resilience training, explore external
support for financial advice, and use part of the Fund to assist
with hoarding cases were also noted. A separate application process
for heating?oil support was proposed, reflecting increased fuel
costs and aligned with existing affordable?warmth criteria.
 

 
Committee
acknowledged that the scheme would be kept under review to ensure
it met local need effectively.

 

RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:

 

1.         Delegate
authority to the Director of Economic Development and Planning to
implement a Crisis and Resilience Fund for the Borough in
accordance with Section 11 of the report.

 

2.         Require the
Director of Economic Development and Planning to provide regular
updates on CRF to Committee.
topline: The Director of Economic Development and Planning has decided to implement a Crisis and Resilience Fund to support low-income households in the Borough.

The Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report outlining recent
developments concerning the Council’s Internal Audit Service
and providing Members with proposals for the future provision of
the service so as to ensure the effective continuation of an
internal audit function.
 
It was noted that
the Council currently operate an in-house internal audit service,
although this is currently being provided by MIAA due to recurring
recruitment issues.
 
There have been
recruitment issues for a number of years and following a recent
resignation the Council are in a position where all posts are
vacant within the team. The exception is the Internal Audit
Assistant post which had been repurposed to undertake the non-audit
duties that fell to the Internal Audit team.
 
The Council is
required to have an internal audit function, but there are options
for this to be provided in-house, outsourced or through shared
services. The report sought approval for outsourcing of the
internal audit function. This should address issues of resilience
and ensure access to a wider base of audit skills and knowledge.
The impending Local Government Reorganisation also has a weighting
on the reasons for the suggestion of outsourcing the service.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the
outsourcing of the council’s Internal Audit service.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report updating Committee on the
Clitheroe Market improvements and to seek approval for further
improvements to the market area.
 
With a total
capital budget of £747,430 available, the Director of
Economic Development and Planning, along with the Working Group had
considered several options to enhance the market’s
appearance, accessibility, safety and footfall. Initial proposals
included new planters, bins, and benches, alongside potential
replacement of roller shutters. Wider strategic suggestions
included improved signage and wayfinding, as well as a detailed
assessment of active travel connections to the town, urban greening
interventions, and potential living wall installations.
 
Further
improvements were also proposed to address operational issues,
health and safety concerns, and compliance with Martyn’s Law.
These included installing removable bollards at the end of New
Market Street to control vehicle access, resurfacing certain areas,
creating improved bin storage, and installing new permanent cabins
along New Market Street.
 
Councillors D Birtwhistle and M French
were granted permission to speak.
 
Councillor Birtwhistle expressed his
disappointment with most of the recommendations made in the
report.  He felt that further
improvements need to be made to the Bull Ring and suggested a
different approach should be taken, for example utilising modular
structures.
 
Councillor French
supported some recommendations, such as signage, but raised
concerns regarding the proposed cabins extending beyond the current
market footprint. He
suggested removal of some of the casual stalls on the Bull Ring,
replacing them with more permanent modular structures.
 
The Director of
Economic Development and Planning then updated Members as to a
meeting held with market traders on 17 March as to the proposed
improvements.  The traders who attended
had expressed several concerns, including the belief that four
proposed cabins at the back of the market would not attract
footfall and access issues around Cabin 3. They wanted parking to
remain on a first?come?first?served basis and raised concerns about
delivery access on non?market days. Suggestions were made to
relocate the Horse Box, add new cabins in the Bull Ring area,
install a roof over cabins, improve planting and signage, and
upgrade roller shutters to electric versions. 
 
A revised market
plan was been presented to the market traders which does introduce
a proposal to replace several casual stalls with two permanent
cabins. This updated plan was put forward for Members to
consider.

Committee was asked
to approve minor works, give direction on larger items such as
shutters and greening options, commission consultants for the
active travel work, and support progressing access and safety
improvements.
 
Committee Members then discussed the
proposals in detail.  Concerns
were raised about the effectiveness of the four permanent stalls on
New Market street and the limited weekday use of casual stalls in
the Bull Ring.  Members expressed less
support for investing in shutters at this stage, and the Director
of Economic Development and Planning will explore this
further.  There was however, strong
support for improving signage, commissioning consultants to help
increase market footfall.  Members also
requested additional information on areas such as indirect greening
and the potential use of modular stalls.
 
RESOLVED THE COMMITTEE:
 

Approve the
initial minor works set out at section 3 of the report and instruct
the Director of Economic Development and Planning to commission
these works to be undertaken asap.

 

The decision on
whether to allocate up to £100,000 for the replacement of the
cabin roller shutters be deferred to enable further
consideration.

 

Note the options
for a bespoke wayfinding solution within the Town. Delegate
authority to the Director of Economic Development and Planning, in
consultation with the Chair of Committee, to develop a suitable
scheme for the Town and secure the necessary permissions.

 

Note the suggested
signage by the local artist for the wall adjacent to the market
entrance and instruct the Director of Economic Development and
Planning to commission the manufacturing of this signage (to be
installed once the wall has been cleaned).

 

Instruct the
Director of Economic Development and Planning to appoint
consultants to undertake an assessment of non-car modes of access
around the wider Town.

 

Instruct the
Director of Economic Development and Planning to proceed in
exploring the option of indirect greening of the car park
wall.

 

Instruct the
Director of Economic Development and Planning to proceed in
exploring the option of urban planting within the car park.

 

Instruct the
Director of Economic Development and Planning to seek quotes (or
formal tender) for the improvements set out at section 5 of the
report (with the layout as per the version attached to the market
traders meeting minutes (17/03/2026) and to include an option for
modular cabins) and proceed with implementing these improvements
after the food festival. 

 

A further
Clitheroe Market Working Group to be arranged to discuss additional
proposals and suggestions.
topline: The Director of Economic Development and Planning has decided to approve minor works and defer the decision on allocating funds for cabin roller shutters at the Clitheroe Market.
