content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report on the Government’s
significant reforms to the local plan?making system, due to come
into effect from March 2026. The new system introduces a
streamlined 30?month process with mandatory early “getting
ready” stages, Gateway checks, digital?first requirements and
alignment with a revised National Planning Policy Framework
expected in summer 2026.
 
Councils wishing to
complete local plans under the current system must submit by 31
December 2026.  Failure to do so would
mean restarting from the beginning under the new system. The report
outlined that the Council’s current Local Development Scheme
timetable is no longer achievable due to evidence base delays,
staffing challenges, and the scale of national policy changes.
Advice from the Planning Advisory Service (PAS) and an independent
Planning Inspector confirmed that continuing under the existing
system would carry substantial delivery and examination risks.
 
Committee noted
that most preparatory work already undertaken is transferable to
the new plan?making process, and that switching systems would allow
more realistic sequencing, stronger prospects of delivering a sound
Plan, and improved opportunities for public engagement. Members of
the Local Plan Working Group supported transitioning to the new
system, while acknowledging ongoing concerns about exposure to
speculative development given the borough’s current housing
land supply. It was noted that interim housing policy guidance is
proposed to help manage this risk until adoption of the new Local
Plan.
 
The report set out
the implications of both options, the next steps for progressing
work under the new approach, and noted that resource needs,
including staffing, remain critical to timely delivery.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
1.    
Note the emerging details of the new plan making system and
associated guidance.
 
2.    
Agree that work on the Local Plan will be progressed under the new
plan making system (Option B in the report).
 
3.    
Agree to delegate authority to the Director of Economic Development
and Planning, in consultation with the committee Chair, and where
appropriate, seeking the views of the Local Plan Working Group
to: 
 

•       
Approve and publish the Local Plan timetable, attached as Appendix
3, subject to any alterations necessary to ensure alignment of
timings in accordance with the regulations when they come into
force; and 

•       
Publish the formal notice to commence plan making 
 
4.    
Authorise the Director of Economic Development and Planning to
prepare a scoping consultation document to be agreed by this
Committee at a future meeting.
 
5.    
Authorise the Director of Economic Development and Planning to
prepare interim housing policy guidance on housing development to
be agreed in draft form for consultation purposes by this Committee
at a future meeting.
topline: The Director of Economic Development and Planning has decided to transition to a new plan-making system for the local plan in response to government reforms.

The Director of
Economic Development and Planning submitted an urgent report asking
Committee to consider whether the South Lodge, Mitton Road, Whalley
Tree Preservation Order 2025 (TPO) should be confirmed.  Prior
to the meeting, the Chair had agreed to the item being placed on
the agenda for Committee’s consideration for the following
reason. The TPO required confirmation by 10 April 2025, following
the receipt of an objection. Owing to the statutory deadline, the
matter was brought forward for urgent determination as the next
scheduled Committee meeting was not due to take place until 17
April. 
 
Members were
advised that the Order had been made following the unauthorised
topping of three mature pine trees of significant amenity value,
and concerns that further trees on the site were at risk. An
objection to the Order had been submitted. The Countryside Officer
had assessed the trees using the TEMPO methodology and concluded
that protection remained expedient given their age, prominence and
the foreseeable threat of additional works.
 
It was noted that
the landowner had since submitted a professional tree survey and a
Tree Work Application to remove poor?quality trees and replant with
suitable native species, which had been approved. The Committee was
informed that confirming the TPO would ensure the Council could
continue to make informed decisions on the future management of the
retained trees and the replacement planting.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agree to confirm
the South Lodge, Mitton Road, Whalley Tree Preservation Order
2025
topline: The Committee has decided to confirm the South Lodge, Mitton Road, Whalley Tree Preservation Order 2025.

the services had been time limited, therefore staffing was related

The proposals set out in the report had been
discussed the affected staff and funders and would ensure both the
excellent work the staff had done to-date to continue and would
accommodate a new work stream of smoking cessation. As the nature
of the work evolved over the coming months, if an additional post
was seen as the optimum a further report would be brought back to
Committee.
 
The immediate primary concern was the smooth
transition from one funding stream to another and ensuring the
service continued for clients with minimal disruption.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
 
1.     Agreed to
the staffing proposal as set out in the report.
 
2.     Referred a
recommendation to Personnel Committee to approve the following
changes to the Establishment, subject to job evaluation:
 
2.1
The addition of a Part-time Health and Wellbeing Coach at Scale 4
(20 hours per week) for a fixed term of 3 years, and
 
2.2
The addition of a Full-time Health and Wellbeing Coach at Scale 4
for a fixed term of 3 years, funded from the smoking cessation and
healthy weight programmes.
 
2.3
The addition of a P/T Work Stream Lead at Scale 4 (2 days per week)
for a fixed term of 2 years funded from TaAF.
topline: The Community Services has decided to approve staffing proposals for changes to the Health and Wellbeing Team posts.

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a
report to present the recommendations of the working group in
relation to the allocation of grants under Recreation and Culture,
Individual Sporting Excellence and Individual Arts Excellence
awards.
 
The Working Group had met on 25 February 2026
to measure applications received against the qualification criteria
for each award. The report noted that the working group were
impressed with the quality of many of the applications and the
difficulty of allocating limited resource to many deserving
applicants. The recommendations resulted in an underspend on the
Recreation and Culture grants budget, therefore Committee supported
the working group recommendation that £2330 was used to fund
a proposed overspend on the Sporting Excellence awards. Committee
approved  grants totalling
£37,439.50 across the three grant schemes.
 
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Endorsed the recommendations of the working group outlined in
appendices 1 – 3 as attached to the report.
 

2.    
Delegated authority to the Chairman of Community Services Committee
and Director of Community Services to make awards based on the
grant panel recommendations for the remaining budget available for
Recreation and Culture Grants.
 

3.    
Approved the use of £2330 of the remaining Recreation and
Culture budget to fund the difference in the available budget and
awards made for the Sporting Excellence grants.
topline: The Community Services has decided to approve recommendations for the allocation of grants under various award schemes

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a report
informing Committee about advice received in respect of a
compulsory purchase and seeking approval to take preparatory steps
for compulsory purchase.
 
Following a reappraisal of the situation,
external legal advice had been sought and it was proposed that,
subject to the caveats set out in the report, that the Council take
initial preparatory steps towards Compulsory Purchase, which
included procurement of a Land Reference Agent and further external
legal support. As part of the process, the Council would consider
the custodianship of the wells as it moved through the process of
local government reorganisation and formation of unitary
councils.
 
The results of inquiries of the Land Agent
would be reported back to Committee in due course along with
proposals for the next steps to be implemented. The likely costs of
the Land Agent and legal support would be incurred by the Council.
If this could not be met from existing budgets a report would be
taken to Policy and Finance Committee to establish how this could
be funded.
 
Members were pleased to support the proposal
and noted that previous investigations had not identified a
suitable legal route. It was understood that the new route which
had been explored had resulted in new legal advice, therefore
enabling the Council to move forward with the process.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Authorised to the Director of Community
Services to procure the appointment of a Land reference agent and
further legal support necessary to process the preparatory steps
for compulsory acquisition.
topline: The Community Services has decided to proceed with preparatory steps for compulsory acquisition of land.

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a report
seeking Committee’s support for public and stakeholder
consultation on the draft waste strategy for Lancashire prior to
its adoption by all Lancashire Councils later that year. This is
following agreement by Lancashire Leaders and Chief Executives to
proceed to consultation.
 
Adopting a new waste strategy was necessary
for all Lancashire Authorities. It would ensure compliance with the
Environment Act 2021 and prepare the Council for significant
financial and operational changes in the waste sector. Launching
the consultation allowed the council to engage with residents on
the critical changes and ensure the local implementation plan was
robust and responsive to resident’s needs.
 
The report also provided details of the
consultation process, the implications for Ribble Valley of
mandatory service changes, and the incoming financial mechanisms
which would alter the cost base of the waste service.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Supported the public consultation on a new
Waste Strategy for Lancashire.
topline: The Community Services has decided to approve public consultation on a new Waste Strategy for Lancashire.

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a
report updating members on the implementation of the Simpler
Recycling guidelines and seeking committee’s support for a
more proactive targeted approach to encourage recycling.
 
The collection of food waste from all
households would become a statutory requirement in April 2026. Many
Councils had experienced difficulty in procuring the necessary
vehicles in time for the start date. It was now not possible to
implement food waste collections at the required start date and
starting prior to the delivery of vehicles would incur additional
costs. The decision taken by committee to delay the introduction of
food waste was based on a start date of October 2026. Due to the
circumstances outside the Council’s control, following a
rigorous procurement process, it was not possible to start until
February 2027 at the earliest. This had exacerbated the situation
from a reputational perspective but was not thought to increase the
risk of legal challenge. The report provided full details of the
risks of delaying implementation for consideration.
 
The Government had not allocated specific
funding for food waste collections as previously expected, instead
it had been included within the Council’s general grant
settlement. Funding overall had been reduced and therefore there
had been no additional funding for food waste collections.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agreed to implementing Food Waste Collections
from February 2027 due to circumstances outside the Councils’
control.
topline: The Community Services department has decided to delay the implementation of food waste collections until February 2027.

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a report
seeking Committee approval to set the charge for the
Salthill staff car park at £50 per annum.
 
Following Committee approval in August 2025,
the parking order had now been through the necessary consultation
and was in place. Salthill Depot car park was now designated as a
car park, and permits could be issued to council staff as well as a
parking fine for non-permitted cars.
 
The rationale for the suggested annual charge of £50
was included for Member’s consideration. Members spoke for
and against the introduction of the annual charge and concerns were
raised regarding the impact on affected staff and the lack of safe
alternative routes of travel to the depot. Committee therefore
requested that the arrangement be reviewed in 3 months-time, and
that staff be consulted.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Authorised the Director of Community Services to put in place a
staff car parking scheme for the recently designated car park at
Salthill Depot based on an annual charge of £50.
 

2.    
Requested a review of
the arrangement, in consultation with the affected staff, after a
period of three months.
topline: The Community Services has decided to set the charge for the Salthill staff car park at £50 per annum

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report seeking approval from members for the
proposed four-year capital programme covering the period 2026/27 to
2029/30 and asking Committee to recommend a capital programme to
Full Council on 3 March 2026.
 
A review of all the existing approved schemes
had been undertaken by Heads of Service, and no further changes
were proposed as a result of the review.
 
The Ribblesdale Pool Refurbishment scheme was
included in the capital programme at a cost of £3m. The
report explained that extra budget of £1.225m had been
requested in order to undertake additional works on the pool lining
and pool. The Budget Working Group supported the proposal and for
the additional budget to be financed by the transfer from general
fund balances.
  
Following a meeting of Budget Working Group on
the 10 February 2026, there had been a number of further amendments
to the programme proposed:
 

·      
Budget Working Group proposed that £100,000 be added to the
2026/27 capital programme for solar panels at Ribblesdale Pool,
although it was recognised that further work was needed by officers
to finalise likely costs.

·      
Indicative costs had been received for the Cemetery Extension, as
agreed at Health and Housing Committee on 16 January 2025. Budget
Working Group proposed that a capital scheme be added in to the
2026/27 capital programme for £450,000, based on the
indicative costs.

·      
Budget Working Group supported the proposal for £500,000 to
be added to the Health and Housing capital programme split as
£250,000 for the renovation of the Joiners Arms property and
£250,000 as an additional amount towards Clitheroe Market
Improvements.
 
The Budget Working Group supported these
schemes being funded from General Fund Balances. These additions
resulted in a capital programme for 2026/27 to 2029/30 totalling
£16,961,680.
 
Full details of the resulting proposed
four-year capital programme were provided in the Annex to the
report for Members consideration.
 
The report noted that in regard to capital
programme proposals beyond 2029/30, it was recommended that no
further years be added. Heads of Service had instead been asked to
identify essential capital schemes or items that were necessary for
the continuation of ‘business as usual’ so that they
can be separately noted.
 
Councillor L Street returned to the meeting
during the report.
 
Members thanked Officers for the updated
report and supported the proposed additions by the Budget Working
Group.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Recommended to Council the Capital Programme
for 2026/27 to 2029/30 as set out in the Annex to the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to recommend a four-year capital programme covering the period 2026/27 to 2029/30, including additional budget requests for various projects.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report for Committee to consider and approve
the Council’s overall revised capital programme for
2025/26.
 
The original programme had been approved by
Council in March 2025, and regular reports had been presented to
all committees on progress with the schemes. There had been a
number of further approvals and adjustments made during the
year resulting in the total approved Capital Programme for 2025/26
of £16,225,175 over seventy-two schemes. The revised estimate
for each of these schemes had been determined following discussion
with budget holders regarding their progress and estimated full
year expenditure.
 
The revised Capital Programme now stood at
£7,639 475 for sixty-eight schemes, which was a reduction of
£8,585,700 from the previously approved capital programme
budget and a net reduction of four schemes. The majority of this
was accounted for by schemes moving to the 2026/27. Details around
the movements were provided in the report.
 
The report went on to outline how the capital
programme had been financed. Earmarked reserves were used to fund
£3,585,940 of the 2025/26 proposed revised capital programme,
with the balance of the funding coming from usable capital receipts
of £154,940, borrowing £500,000 together with grants
and contributions of £3,398,595.
 
Cllr L Street left the meeting during the
report.
  
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the overall revised capital programme
for 2025/26.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the Council's revised capital programme for 2025/26.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report asking Committee to approve the
revised Revenue Budget for 2025/26 and to recommend a revenue
budget and council tax requirement for 2026/27 to Council on 3
March 2026.
 
Cllr J Rogerson entered the meeting during the
report.
 
The revised budget forecasted that instead of
adding £307k from general fund balances as originally
planned, £564k would be added. Service Committees had
considered their detailed reports and main variations between the
original and revised estimate were provided in Annex 1 to the
report.
 
A significant element of the Council’s
income was Business Rate Growth, and the report outlined the latest
estimate of Ribble Valley’s share of business rate income for
the current year. Based on the latest position the Council income
from business rates was expected to be £2.735m after many
adjustments. This was only slightly less than the amount originally
estimated of £2.768m. For 2025/26 £2m was relied upon
to fund the revenue budget, with the business rate growth reserve
being used to fund the capital programme over the next 5 years.
 
The report detailed the forecasted transfers
to and from earmarked reserves compared with the original estimate,
and in summary, the net position was that £2.268m would be
added instead of £543k to earmarked reserves in the current
year. One of the largest variations was £1.304m of section
106 monies which had been received into the service revenue budget,
however it had previously been agreed that this would be used to
finance part of the capital programme. As such, these monies had
been set aside in the Capital Earmarked Reserve, therefore had an
overall net nil impact on the revenue budget.
  
The report went on to highlight the key
elements of the Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement
2026/27, in summary:
 

·      
The new Fair Funding Allocation will be phased in over the next 3
years, with the Council receiving:
 ?
2026/27 = 1/3 new FFA allocation + 2/3 of the previous
allocation
 ?
2027/28 = 2/3 new FFA allocation + 1/3 of the previous
allocation
 ?
2028/29 = the new FFA allocation in full
 

·      
The Council would receive a damping payment each year to ensure the
allocation was not less than 95% of the adjusted allocation for
2025/26, which included some grants that had been ‘rolled
in’ which were previously paid separately.
 

·      
The Business Rates Baseline had been reset
 
Given many uncertainties, including the impact
of the new 2026 rating list, and the new Business Rates Baselines
(not announced until the provisional grant settlement), the new
banded levy calculation and how this would work in a new pool, it
was felt the risks were too high to be a member of a business rates
pool in 2026/27.
  
The Director of Resources estimated that the
Collection Fund would produce an overall surplus of £360,406
for 2026/27. This consisted of a surplus for council tax of
£467,802 and a deficit in respect of Business Rates of
£107,396. The Council Tax surplus would be shared amongst all
the major precepting authorities in 2026/27, with the
Council’s share of the surplus being £40,007.
 
Regarding the revenue budget for 2026/27, the
report outlined the provisional base position as agreed by Service
Committees. Committee expenditure was set to increase by
£673k, the reasons for which were set out for each Committee
in the annex to the report. Capital adjustments and movements of
other items were also reported. At this stage, a contingency of
£400k was included for Local Government Reorganisation
transition costs.
 
In an addendum to the report, Members were
informed that the Government had announced the Final Local
Government Grant Settlement on 9 February 2026 which contained some
significant changes from the Provisional Local Government Finance
Settlement published in December. The addendum summarised the key
changes and the impact on the Council was as follows:
 
·      
Extra funding for Homelessness, Rough Sleeping and Domestic Abuse
would result in extra amounts as follows: £22k in 2026/27;
£16k in 2027/28 and £13k in 2028/29. These would not
impact on the budget deficit as they would be used to fund extra
expenditure that met the intention of the funding.
·      
The Government had reconsidered the allocation of pooling gains and
they would be shared 50:50 between tariff and top up authorities
resulting in Ribble Valley BC being £466k each year worse off
compared with the provisional settlement. However, a one-year
one-off Adjustment Support Grant of £466k would be received
for 2026/27 only.
 
The budget forecast had been updated following
the release of the Final Local Government Grant Settlement and this
predicted the following budget shortfalls each year:
 





 



Budget Gap

0

1,147,520

It was pointed out that this was after the
assumption that £250k would be taken from general fund
balances each year.
 
The Budget Working Group had met throughout
the year and on 10 February 2026 to consider the Council’s
latest financial position, the impact of the Final Grant
Settlement, and some further budget items. They had made the
following recommendations for approval by Committee:
 

·      
Increase the Council’s Band D Council Tax by 2.99% to
£175.79

·      
To bring in £791k of Extended Producer Responsibility Funding
for each year of the future forecast.

·      
To monitor closely interest rate changes during the year and
capital spending.

·      
That the request from Community Services Committee for extra
funding for the Pool Refurbishment Capital scheme is approved at
£1.240m and funded from general fund balances.

·      
That £100k is added to the capital programme to fund solar
panels at Ribblesdale Pool.

·      
The further use of General Fund Balances to support the Ash Dieback
Management growth item at a cost of £100k over 3 years.

·      
That £450k is added to the four-year capital programme for
the Cemetery Extension funded from General Fund Balances.

·      
That £500k is added to the four-year capital programme for
the Joiners Arms and Clitheroe Market Improvements funded from
General Fund Balances.

·      
That the resulting revised budget gap of £145,000 is taken
from general fund balances in 2026/27.

·      
Given the significant forecast deficit for future years, the
financial pressures and remaining uncertainties the Budget Working
Group recommend that they should continue to meet on a regular
basis to review the budget position and assess how the budget gaps
in years 2027/28 onwards should be addressed.
  
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive, as the Section 151 Officer, presented her report set out
in Annex 7 which was required under Section 25 of the Local
Government Finance Act 2003 to consider the robustness of the
budget and the adequacy of the Council’s balances and
reserves.  She concluded that the budget estimates for
2026/27 were robust, and the level of reserves and balances
adequate.  However, it was stressed that the Council
faced significant budget gaps beyond 2026/27. Whilst the level of
General Fund Balances and Earmarked Reserves was relatively high,
the use of reserves to fund budget gaps was not sustainable. She
recommended that the Budget Working Group consider steps to address
how a balanced budget could be set beyond 2026/27 as soon as
practicable.
 
Committee were asked to consider the
recommendations which would result in a balanced budget for
2026/27, as set out in the report.
 
The recommendation at 11.1 of the report was
proposed and seconded. A vote was taken and the motion was
carried.
 
Councillor K Horkin spoke against the Budget
Working Group’s recommendation to increase Council Tax and
proposed an amendment that the current Council Tax
Band D equivalent remained at £170.69 and was not increased
by 2.99%, to be funded from the unexpected savings generated by the
reduction in superannuation payments of £177,000 as noted the
report at 6.20. The impact of the increase on the revenue budget
would be £131,850 for 2026/27.
 
The amendment was seconded by
Councillor S Bibby.
 
Members debated the amendment and spoke both
for and against the proposal.
 
A vote was taken and that was carried
therefore this became the substantive
motion.
 
Officers confirmed
that the resulting revised budget gap for 2026/27 was
£277k.
 
Councillor S Hirst proposed the recommendation
at 11.2 of the report to approve recommendations of the working
group, with the exception of the increase to Council Tax which
should remain at £170.69 for a Band D property. Councillor M
Hindle seconded the motion with the same exception. A vote was
taken and the motion was carried.
 
The recommendations at 11.3 and 11.4 of the
report were proposed and seconded. Separate votes were taken and
the motions carried. It was therefore:
 
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
1.      
Approved the revised budget for 2025/26.

 

2.       Approved the Budget Working Group’s recommendations set
out in Section 8 of the report, with the exception of the increase
to Council Tax which should remain at £170.69 for a Band D
property and the difference be funded from general fund balances,

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report for information providing details of
the Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement.
 
On 20 November 2025 the Ministry of Housing,
Communities and Local Government (MHCLG) published a Policy
Statement which set out the government’s intentions for the
Local Government Finance Settlement. The Policy Statement set out
the Government’s intention to include pooling gains within
transitional protection arrangements, which would mean a
significant improvement in the Council’s funding position in
comparison to the indications arising from the Fair Funding 2.0
consultation. MHCLG also stated that revenue funding for Weekly
Food Waste collection would be ‘rolled in’ to the grant
settlement. 
 
The Provisional Local Government Grant
Settlement for 2026/27 to 2028/29 had been published on 17 December
2025. The Provisional Finance Settlement set out the
Council’s detailed funding for the forthcoming 3 years. This
confirmed the transitional protection arrangements in the Policy
Statement. For Ribble Valley, the Damping Payment would be
£195k for 2026/27, £965k in 2027/28 rising to
£1.8m in 2028/29 the final year of the multi-year settlement
to compensate for the phased reduction in Settlement Funding
Assessment. There was no indication of what would happen beyond
this period. The report noted:
 

·      
It was disappointing that Food Waste funding had been rolled in to
the grant settlement.

·      
The inclusion of pooling gains resulted in far better protection
arrangements for Ribble Valley BC.

·      
There would be a cliff edge potentially after 2028/29.

·      
At this stage we assume we will receive Extended Producer
Responsibility funding at the same level as the current year i.e.
£792k for each year.
 
A consultation
period ran until 14 January 2026. The Council had responded to the
consultation setting out the importance of the announced protection
arrangements.
 
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive informed members that the
Final Local Government Finance Settlement had since been announced
and further information was given in the following report.
topline: The Policy and Finance has decided to improve Ribble Valley's funding position through the Provisional Local Government Finance Settlement, including transitional protection arrangements and funding for Weekly Food Waste collection.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and Planning submitted
a report updating Committee on a consultation recently
published by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local
Government (MHCLG) relating to reforms to the National Planning
Policy Framework and other changes to the planning system. The
deadline for responses to the consultation was 10th March 2026.
 
The preamble to the consultation stated that
the government was committed to tackling the country’s
housing crisis. As such the consultation invited views on
significant structural improvements to the Framework, as well as
how they could most effectively manage a potential transition from
the current non-statutory approach to the introduction of statutory
National Development Management Policies.
 
The twelve most significant reforms were
summarised as follows:
 

1.    
A permanent presumption in favour of suitably located
development.

2.    
Building homes around stations.

3.    
Driving urban and suburban densification.

4.    
Securing a diverse mix of homes.

5.    
Supporting small and medium sites.

6.    
Streamlining local standards.

7.    
Boosting local and regional economies.

8.    
Supporting critical and growth minerals.

9.    
Embedding a vision-led approach to transport.

10. 
Better addressing climate change.

11. 
Conserving and enhancing the natural environment.

12. 
Taking a more positive approach to the use of heritage assets.
 
The questions were appended to the report with
suggested responses provided for Committee approval.
 
At the meeting, Members discussed flooding
concerns and development around train stations and put forward
suggestions to be incorporated into the responses. Members
supported the consultation response and thanked Officers for the
detailed report.
 
Councillor M Graveston left and returned to
the meeting during the debate.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Noted the proposed reforms and authorised the Director of Economic
Development and Planning to submit a response to the consultation
based on the suggested answers attached at Appendix 1 to the
report.
 

2.    
Approved that authority be delegated to the Director of Economic
Development and Planning, in consultation with the Chair of P&D
Committee, to undertake drafting of any minor
amendments/updates required to the Council’s consultation
response prior to submission.
topline: The Planning and Development Committee has decided to approve recommendations for reforms to the National Planning Policy Framework and other changes to the planning system.

content:
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
The Applicant’s Agent, Ms K Delaney
spoke in support of the application.
 
REFUSE planning permission for the following
reasons:-
 

1.    
The proposed development would result in the introduction of an
incongruous and discordant form of development within the Open
Countryside that fails to respond positively to the inherent
character of the area contrary to Policies DMG1 and DMG2 of the
Ribble Valley Core Strategy and paragraph 187 of the National
Planning Policy Framework.
 

2.    
The proposed development would represent poor design, by virtue of
the cramped grid layout with insufficient spacing between buildings
and between buildings and the street, dominance of frontage
parking, hard development edges, lack of architectural detailing
and variety, lack of useable and accessible public open space, and
failure to give due consideration to protected trees on and
adjacent to the site. This is contrary to Policies DMG1, DMB4 and
DME1 of the Ribble Valley Core Strategy and paragraph 135 (a-f) of
the National Planning Policy Framework.
 

3.    
The proposed development would not sustain an appropriate mix of
housing, in particular the application fails to demonstrate how the
requirement for older persons accommodation would be met. This is
contrary to Key Statements H2 and H3 and Policy DMH1 of the Ribble
Valley Core Strategy.
 

4.    
The site is at risk of surface water flooding and the application
has failed to demonstrate that an appropriate sustainable drainage
strategy can be achieved on the site contrary to Policy DME6 of the
Ribble Valley Core Strategy and paragraph 182 of the National
Planning Policy Framework.
 

5.    
The applicant has failed to demonstrate that future users of the
development would not be at risk from unacceptable road noise
levels associated with the adjacent A59 and Clitheroe Road. This is
contrary to Policy DMG1 of the Ribble Valley Core Strategy and
paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework.
 

6.    
The proposed development would result in the loss of existing
habitat and individual trees, with insufficient details being
submitted to demonstrate an appropriate strategy for achieving the
statutory requirement for Biodiversity Net Gain contrary to
Schedule 7A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (inserted by
the Environment Act 2021).
topline: The Planning and Development Committee has decided to refuse planning permission for a proposed development in the Open Countryside.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report seeking authority from Committee in
respect of a Service Level Agreement with LCC for archaeological
advice for the period 2026-27.
 
A proposed SLA had been issued by LCC to RVBC
for 2026/27 for a fee of £11,516, a copy of which was
appended to the report. The costs were proportioned across the
receiving Lancashire authorities based on anticipated use of the
service. As well as assessing all planning applications requiring
ground disturbance via the weekly list, the SLA included provision
for the Historic Environment Team to assess historic building
applications, development consent order (DCO) projects, provide
input to policy (local plans, land allocations, neighbourhood plans
etc) and importantly, maintain, manage and enhance the Lancashire
Historic Environment Record (HER).
 
LCC remained committed to reviewing the
existing charging system towards the end of the current 3-year
cycle to ensure it remained proportionally fair when setting new
fees for the next 3-year cycle 2027-2030. Updated statistics on
usage would be monitored by officers to inform the decision on
entering into future SLAs, which would be brought to Committee at a
later date. In the meantime, it was considered that entering into a
SLA with LCC for 2026/27 would be the most appropriate course of
action to allow RVBC to continue to benefit from the archaeology
advice it received from LCC and meet the requirements of the NPPF
both in terms of sound decision taking and plan making.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the Council entering into a Service
Level Agreement with Lancashire County Council (LCC) for the
provision of Archaeological advice for 2026/27 and pay the invoice
of £11,516 for that period when issued by LCC.
topline: The Planning and Development Committee has decided to approve the Council entering into a Service Level Agreement with Lancashire County Council for archaeological advice for the period 2026-27.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report informing Committee about steps which
needed to be taken to address Ash Dieback affecting trees on the
Council’s land.
 
RVBC had been managing the impact of Ash
Dieback in recent years on numerous Council owned sites across the
Borough, removing trees where necessary. Prior to 2024/25, the
works had been completed within existing budgetary provisions.
Subsequently, due to the significant amounts of works required,
supplementary budgets were then approved by Policy and Finance
Committee for works totalling:
 

·      
£31,950 in 2024/25

·      
£25,380 in 2025/26
 
Ash Dieback was proving a very fluid disease
to manage and any tree work carried out so far would not be the end
of the process. Further felling of dead, dying and diseased ash
trees would have to be carried out over at least 3 years until the
threat of tree failure was reduced to an acceptable level of
risk.
 
Officers had undertaken risk assessments and
tree counts on sixty-five Council owned sites. Taking account of
the works undertaken already and a worst-case scenario of the works
required over the coming 3 years, the calculations resulted in an
estimated total contract value of over £100,000, as such a
formal tender exercise would be required.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Referred to Policy and Finance Committee a
request for a growth item of £100,000 to manage Ash Dieback
on Council owned sites for 3 years between 2026/27-2028/29.
topline: The Planning and Development Committee has approved recommendations to address Ash Dieback affecting trees on Council owned sites.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and
Planning submitted a report seeking approval of an exemption from
the requirements of the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules,
under CPR 5.2(e), to enable the urgent instruction and direct award
of contract to consultants to provide a Green Belt Review
(Incorporating Grey Belt Assessment). The study would form a
critical part of the evidence base informing the ongoing
preparation of the Local Plan.
 
Whilst a compliant and transparent ITQ process
had been undertaken, in accordance with CPR6, only one quotation
was received. An exemption from the requirements of the
Council’s Contract Procedure Rules was therefore requested in
order to proceed with the appointment.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the request for an exemption from the
requirements of the Council’s Contract Procedure Rules, under
CPR 5.2(e), on the basis that a compliant procurement exercise was
undertaken; a single compliant quotation was received; value for
money and compliance with domestic legislation had been
demonstrated; and re-tendering would cause delay without a
reasonable expectation of increased competition.
topline: The Planning and Development has decided to approve an exemption from the Council's Contract Procedure Rules to urgently award a contract for a Green Belt Review.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive submitted a report which
included the Letter of Representation for 2024/25 Statement of
Accounts that Grant Thornton had required to be signed before they
could sign off the accounts.
 
The letter set out
assurances from the Council to Grant Thornton that relevant
accounting standards had been complied with and gave further
assurances that the Council had disclosed information, which if it
was withheld, would undermine the accuracy and reliability of the
Statement of Accounts.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the letter
of representation to Grant Thornton in respect of the 2024/25
Statement of Accounts.
topline: The Accounts and Audit Committee has decided to approve a letter of representation to Grant Thornton for the 2024/25 Statement of Accounts.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive submitted a report providing
an update to Committee in respect of progress made in delivery
against 2025/26 Internal Audit Plan. The report outlined a summary
of internal audit activity which was a requirement of the Global
Internal Audit Standards (GIAS).
 
It was noted that
there were currently four audits where work of varying degrees was
being undertaken.
 
Members were
advised that resourcing issues within the Internal Audit function
have impacted the delivery of audits scheduled in the 2025/26
Internal Audit Plan. To support an informed Head of Internal Audit
Opinion for 2025/26, the Council was seeking to outsource selected
audits.
topline: The Accounts and Audit has decided to outsource selected audits to address resourcing issues within the Internal Audit function.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive submitted a report informing
Committee of the statutory requirement to close down the
Council’s accounts by 30 June 2026.
 
A detailed
timetable was annexed to the report setting out the required
actions, with the persons responsible for each task. Members were
reminded that it was imperative that the accounts for the current
year were closed as soon as reasonably practicable in order to
inform the budget setting process for future years. This allowed
the Council to be able to consider its reserves and balances and
areas of over/under spending with greater certainty.
 
The report noted
that the Accounts and Audit (Amendment) Regulations 2024 had
amended the deadline for the publication of the Council’s
draft ‘accountability statements’ from 31 May to 30
June, which had been incorporated into the timetable.
 
The exact timing of
the external audit was not yet known, however this would be
reflected in the timetable once the Council were
notified. 
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Endorsed the
suggested approach for the closure of the 2025/26 accounts.
topline: The Accounts and Audit has decided to endorse the approach for closing the Council's accounts by 30 June 2026.

content:
Grant Thornton
submitted their Annual Report on Ribble Valley Borough Council
covering the period up to 31 March 2025.
 
This report brought
together a summary of all the work Grant Thornton had undertaken
for RBVC during 2024/25 as the appointed external auditor. The core
element of the report was the commentary on the Value for Money
(VfM) arrangements. The responsibilities of the Council were set
out in Appendix A and the Value for
Money Auditor responsibilities were set out in Appendix B of the
report.
 
The Chairman
thanked Grant Thornton for their work.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Accept the
Auditor’s Annual Report for the year ending 31 March 2025
topline: The Accounts and Audit Committee has decided to accept Grant Thornton's Annual Report for Ribble Valley Borough Council.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy
Chief Executive submitted a report outlining developments
concerning the Council’s Internal Audit Service and
providing members with proposals for the future provision of the
service so as to ensure the effective
continuation of an internal audit function.
 
The council
operated an in-house internal audit service. There had been
recruitment issues for a number of years
and following a recent resignation the Council were in a position
where all posts would be vacant within the team by the end of
February. The council was required to have an internal audit
function, and the report there were options for this to be provided
in-house, outsourced or through shared services. The report
suggested that consideration was given to the internal audit
function being outsourced which should address issues of resilience
and ensure access to a wider base of audit skills and knowledge.
The impending Local Government Reorganisation had a weighting on
the suggestion of outsourcing the service.
 
These proposals
were reported for information purposes for this and it was planned to take a decision report to
Policy and Finance Committee on 31 March 2026.
topline: The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief Executive has decided to outsource the Council's Internal Audit Service.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive submitted a report asking
Committee to formally approve the Statement of Accounts for 2024/25
following completion of the audit.
 
The Head of
Financial Services reminded Members that their role in approving
the Statement of Accounts, following the conclusion of the audit,
was to confirm their ownership of the statements, their confidence
in the Section 151 Officer and the robustness of the process by
which accounting records were maintained and the statements
prepared.
 
He reported
that:
·      
The draft Statement of Accounts (subject to Audit) had been made
available on the Council’s website on 30 June 2025.
·      
The final outturn on the general fund revenue account was a surplus
of £1.186m rather than the £579k surplus forecast at
the revised estimate.
·      
There had also been £2,351,895 (revenue only) added to
earmarked reserves at year end rather than the revised estimate
forecast of £1,460,998 to be added to earmarked reserves. The
difference was largely explained by the items listed at paragraph
3.10 of the report.
·      
After allowing for capital transactions of taking £1,352,392
from earmarked reserves, the overall net movement added to
earmarked reserves was £999,504.
·      
The Collection Fund showed an overall net surplus of
£1.356m.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the
audited Statement of Accounts for 2024/25.
topline: The Accounts and Audit Committee has decided to formally approve the Statement of Accounts for 2024/25.

content:
Elizabeth
Luddington, submitted a report on behalf of Grant Thornton which
outlined their audit findings and key matters arising from the
audit of the Council’s financial statements for the year
ending 31 March 2025.
 
The report reminded
members that, under International Standards of Audit and the
National Audit Office, Grant Thornton were required to report on
whether the Council’s financial statements gave a true and
fair view of the Council’s financial position and its income
and expenditure for the year.
 
Committee was
informed that:
·      
The Audit did not identify any adjustments to the financial
statements that would result in an adjustment to the
Council’s Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Statement.
·      
Several recommendations were made for management, and these were
detailed at pages 39 and 40 of the report.
·      
There were no matters of which the Auditors were aware of that
would require modification or their audit opinion or material
changes to the financial statements subject to the following
outstanding matters:

• receipt of signed management representation letter; and

• review of the final set of signed financial statements
·      
The conclusion is that the other information to be published with
the financial statements, including the Annual Governance
Statement, was consistent with the Auditors knowledge of RVBC and
with the financial statements they had audited.
·      
The anticipated financial statements audit report opinion will be
unmodified.
·      
The Auditor anticipates signing RVBC’s accounts once the
above outstanding matters have been concluded.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Accept the external
auditors audit findings report for year ending 31 March 2025.
topline: The Accounts and Audit committee has decided to accept the external auditors audit findings report for the year ending 31 March 2025.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive provided members with the
Annual Governance review for 2024/25 and sought Committee’s
approval of the resulting Annual Governance Statement.
 
Members were
reminded that all councils were required to prepare an Annual
Governance Statement each year in accordance with the
“Delivering Good Governance in Local Government
Framework” and to publish the extent to which they complied
with their own Local Code of Corporate Governance. The code
included how the Council had monitored the effectiveness of its
governance arrangements in the previous financial year and detailed
any planned changes in the coming period.
 
The report noted
that the Annual Governance Statement was a backward-looking review
of how the Council had performed or acted in relation to the
principles set out at the beginning of the year in its own Local
Code of Corporate Governance.
 
In June 2025 the
Draft Annual Governance Statement was published alongside the
Council’s Draft Statement of Accounts on the Council’s
website, which would be updated to reflect the approval of the
audited Statement of Accounts and the approval of the Annual
Governance Statement.
 
Members were
advised in relation to the issues that had been raised as part of
the Annual Governance Review 2023/24 and their current status. 
Embedding policies and procedures to sustain existing
organisational culture had been fully implemented.  Issues relating to policy reviews, risk
assessments (Health & Safety) and operational risks had been
partially implemented.  It was noted
that over the coming year, steps will be taken to address these
issues to enhance the Council’s governance arrangements.
 
RESOLVED THAT
COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the Annual
Governance Statement 2024/25 as attached to the report.
topline: The Accounts and Audit Committee has decided to approve the Annual Governance Statement for 2024/25.

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a
report seeking Committee’s approval of the proposal
for further conditions on private hire operators’ licences
and consultation on such proposals.
 
Committee was
requested to consider and recommend consultation on two focussed
conditions for operators, which address “out-of-area”
vehicles being sub-contracted by Ribble Valley licensed operators,
and DBS requirements for operators’ staff.
 
A six?week
consultation was proposed, with findings to be reported in March
2026.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Approve
in principle the amendment of the conditions for Private Hire
Operators.
 

2.        
Authorise the Head of Legal and Democratic Services to consult
licence holders and other consultees upon the introduction of the
proposed amendments.
topline: The Chief Executive has decided to approve recommendations for further conditions on private hire operators' licences and consultation on such proposals.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report outlining the draft revenue budget for
2026/27, for approval by committee and then consideration at
Special Policy and Finance committee.
 
The report detailed the major changes which
had now been confirmed following the Government’s Fair
Funding Consultation. The report also set out:

The provisional local government
finance settlement.
The impact on the Council of the
Government’s significant local government finance
reforms
The budget process and how the
estimates were prepared.
The draft revenue budget for 2026/27
and the main variations.

 
The Provisional Finance Settlement had
confirmed the transitional protection arrangements in the Policy
Statement. For Ribble Valley, the Damping Payment would be
£195k for 2026/27, £965k in 2027/28 rising to
£1.8m in 2028/29, the final year of the multi-year
settlement. There was no indication of what would happen beyond
that period. The Final Settlement was expected in early February
2026.
 
The Budget Working Group would continue to
meet frequently and assess the draft overall position in mid
January, when all service committee budgets will had been
considered.
 
The guidance from Policy and Finance Committee
to service committees was to manage their services from within
their existing budgets, finding savings to fund any growth items
where possible. It was also recommended that fees and charges were
increased on average by 2.5%.
 
The difference between the Original Estimate
2025/26 and proposed Original Estimate 2026/27 was a decrease in
net expenditure of £7,460.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the revenue original estimate for
2026/27 and to submit it to the Special Policy and Finance
Committee.
topline: The Economic Development council has decided to approve the draft revenue budget for 2026/27.

content:
Apologies for absence were received from Councillor J
Atherton.
topline: The council has decided to approve the recommendations.

content:
RESOLVED: Committee resolved to vary the order
of the agenda therefore Agenda Item 6 – Revised Revenue
Budget 2025/26 was taken before Agenda Item 5 – Original
Revenue Budget 2026/27.
 
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report asking committee to agree a revised
revenue budget for 2025/26 for this committee.
 
Members were reminded that at this time of
year the estimates were revised for the current financial year in
order to predict the likely outturn. In essence the revised
estimate was the Council’s latest forecast for the outturn on
the current financial year’s budget. This also assisted the
Council in preparing the original estimates for the coming
financial year.
 
The original budget for 2025/26 included the
provision for pay increases at 4% and price increases at 2.5%. The
pay award for 2025/26 had now been settled at 3.2% per full time
employee which was slightly lower than the 4% budgeted for. There
had been detailed discussions with budget holders and heads of
service, with past service provision and future plans both playing
an important part in the budget setting process. Committee
decisions during the year had also been incorporated into the
budget setting process where appropriate.
 
A comparison between the revised and original
estimates, and detailed analysis of the variances, was included in
the report. The difference between the Original Estimate and
Revised Estimate was an increase in net expenditure of
£76,670.
 
Members discussed the empty units at Albion
Mill and the high ongoing revenue costs. A report would be brought
back to a future Committee detailing the options for Member’s
consideration.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agreed the revenue Revised Estimate for
2025/26.
topline: The Economic Development has decided to vary the agenda order to discuss the revised revenue budget for 2025/26 before the original budget for 2026/27.

content:
The minutes of the meeting held on 20 November
2025 were approved as a correct record and signed by the
Chairman.
topline: The council has decided to approve the minutes from a meeting held on 20 November 2025

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a report for
Committee to approve the proposed updated
Terms of Reference (ToR) for the Climate Emergency Working Group in
light of the Motion: Declaration of a Climate Emergency, agreed by
Council on 14 October 2025, and to agree the proposed amended
wording of the Climate Change Declaration on the Council
website.
 
Following consideration at their meeting on 15 January
2026, the Working Group had recommended proposed amendments to both
the ToR and declaration, which were provided for Committee’s
approval.
 
At the meeting, Members were pleased with the revised
wording of the declaration. In regard to the ToR, Members put
forward some minor amendments which would be incorporated.
Committee also supported a proposal that Cllrs K Horkin and J
Alcock be replaced on the Working Group by Cllrs S Hore and R
Walsh.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved the Climate Emergency Working Group Terms
of Reference at Appendix 1 subject to the minor amendments as
discussed which would be incorporated.
 

2.    
Agreed to the change of wording of the Climate
Emergency Declaration on the Council website at Appendix
2.
 

3.    
Approved that Cllrs J Alcock and K Horkin be
replaced on the Climate Emergency Working Group by Cllrs S Hore and
R Walsh.
topline: The Economic Development has decided to approve updated Terms of Reference for the Climate Emergency Working Group and amend the Climate Change Declaration on the Council website.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report for Committee to agree the
Council’s Corporate Debt Policy (CDP).
 
The Council was required to collect debts
across several different departments. These debts could be in
relation to a variety of services, ranging from Business Rates,
Council Tax and rent for both commercial and residential
properties. The revised policy did not make any significant changes
to the existing policy; it included additional information and
explanation to ensure that all debt recovery actions were
transparent and fair.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the Corporate Debt Policy attached at
Annex 1 to the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the Council's Corporate Debt Policy for debt collection.

content:
The Director of Community Services submitted a
report seeking committee’s support for a decision made by
Community Committee in May 2025 to utilise the Atrium Café
space at the museum as a cultural space rather than as a commercial
café concession. Despite significant effort, including
research, soft marketing and a formal tender process it had not
been possible to source a sustainable operator.
 
Members discussed the café and its
poignant position next to the Castle. Considering the significant
ongoing works to the Castle Keep and Grounds, Committee recommended
to Community Services Committee that the arrangements be seen as
temporary and therefore be reconsidered at a future date.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Agreed that the income budget for the Atrium café concession
of £17,840 be removed, and an additional income budget for
events be added of £2,000 with effect from 2026/27, due to
the venue now being repurposed as a cultural space.
 

2.    
Refer to Community Committee, that this be considered as a
temporary arrangement in order for options for the Atrium
café to be reconsidered at a future date.
topline: The Policy and Finance committee has decided to repurpose the Atrium Café space at the museum as a cultural space rather than a commercial café concession.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report seeking approval of a revised revenue
budget for 2025/26.
 
Members were reminded that the original
estimate for the current financial year was set in March 2025. At
this time of year, the Council revised the estimates for the
current financial year to predict the likely outturn.
 
The report noted that:

·      
The pay award for 2025/26 had been settled at 3.2% which was
slightly lower than the 4% allowed for.

·      
There had been detailed discussions with budget holders and heads
of service on past service provision and future plans, both playing
an important part in the budget setting process.

·      
Committee decisions during the year had been incorporated into the
budget setting process where appropriate.

·      
The overall difference between the Revised and Original Estimate
was a decrease in net expenditure of £11,980 or a decrease in
net expenditure of £2,490 after allowing for transfers to and
from earmarked reserves.
 
Detailed information was provided on the
variances.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Agreed the revenue revised estimate for
2025/26.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve a revised revenue budget for 2025/26.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report outlining the draft revenue budget for
2026/27, for approval by committee and then consideration at
Special Policy and Finance committee.
 
Members were reminded that the budget forecast
was presented to Committee in September 2025, The Budget Working
Group had continued to meet frequently and would assess the draft
overall position in mid-January, when all service committee budgets
had been considered. The report set out:

·      
The provisional local government finance settlement.

·      
The impact on the Council of the Government’s significant
local government finance reforms

·      
The budget process and how the estimates were prepared.

·      
The draft revenue budget for 206/27 and the main variations.
 
The Provisional Finance Settlement had
confirmed the transitional protection arrangements in the Policy
Statement. For Ribble Valley, the Damping Payment would be
£195k for 2026/27, £965k in 2027/28 rising to
£1.8m in 2028/29, the final year of the multi-year
settlement. There was no indication of what would happen beyond
that period.
 
The guidance from Policy and Finance Committee
to service committees was to manage their services from within
their existing budgets, finding savings to fund any growth items
where possible. It was also recommended that fees and charges were
increased on average by 2.5%.
 
The difference between the Proposed Original
Estimate 2026/27 and Original Estimate 2025/26 was an increase in
net expenditure of £14,800, before allowing for transfers to
and from earmarked reserves, and an increase of £740 after
allowing for transfers to and from earmarked reserves.
 
The small net increase was the result of large
compensating movements across the committee draft budgets. Standard
net inflationary increases of 2.5% would account for estimated
general inflation in respect of pay, prices and income increase
draft budgets by £132k. The increase was more than offset by
additional net inflationary movements that reduced draft budgets by
-£165k, mainly following a reduction to the employers’
pension fund contribution rate.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the revenue original estimate for
2026/27 and to submit it to the Special Policy and Finance
Committee.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the draft revenue budget for 2026/27, with potential contentiousness around managing services within existing budgets and increasing fees and charges.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report asking committee to approve the
2025/26 revised estimate for this Committee’s capital
programme.
 
Six schemes totalling £235,115 had been
approved by Special Policy and Finance committee and Full Council
in February and March 2025 respectively. During the year, slippage
of £202,140 had been approved for four schemes that had not
been completed in the 2024/25 financial year, and one capital
scheme with a budget of £69,760 had been brought forward from
the 2027/28 financial year to 2025/26. The resulting total approved
budget for the Committee’s capital programme of ten schemes
was £770,440.
 
Progress on each of the capital schemes had
been discussed with budget holders, and the capital programme had
been revised to reflect progress and the estimated full year
expenditure for 2025/26. It was recommended that budgets totalling
£216,770 on nine schemes were moved to the 2026/27 financial
year therefore the proposed revised estimate for this
committee’s 2025/26 capital programme was £517,940,
which was a £252,500 reduction from the previously approved
capital budget. At the end of November 2025 £253,190 had been
spent or committed which represented 48.9% of the revised capital
programme for this committee.
 
The Revised Estimate for the Ribble Valley
Shared Prosperity Fund schemes remained unchanged from that
currently approved, therefore the proposed revised estimate was
£1,650,810. At the end of November 2025, £0 had been
spent or committed which represented 0.0% of the revised capital
programme for Ribble Valley Shared Prosperity Fund Schemes.
 
The Revised Estimate for the UKSPF and REPF
schemes remained unchanged from that currently approved, therefore
the proposed revised estimate was £768,575. At the end of
November 2025 £158,659 had been spent or committed which
represented 20.6% of the revised capital programme for UKSPF and
REPF schemes.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.    
Approved the 2025/26 revised estimate of £517,940 for this
Committee’s main capital programme, as set out in Annex 1 of
the report.
 

2.    
Approved the move of the capital scheme budgets shown at paragraph
3.3 of the report from 2025/26 to 2026/27.
 

3.    
Approve the revised estimate of £1,650,810 for the Ribble
Valley Shared Prosperity Fund as set out in Annex 3 of the
report.
 

4.    
Approved the revised estimate of £768,575 for UKSPF and REPF
schemes as set out in Annex 4 of the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve a revised estimate of £517,940 for the 2025/26 capital programme.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report asking committee to consider the
future capital programme for this committee covering the period
2026/27 to 2029/30.
 
Due to the uncertainty regarding the outcome
of the finance reforms and also local government reorganisation, at
their meeting on 16 September 2025, Policy and Finance Committee
gave guidance that no bids for 2030/31 of the capital programme
should be invited, and that the existing programme should be
reviewed for any schemes that could be reprofiled to a later year.
In respect of 2030/31, Heads of Service had instead been asked to
identify essential capital schemes or items that were necessary for
the continuation of ‘business as usual’ so these could
be separately noted.
 
For this committee there had originally been
five schemes approved for the financial years 2026/27 to 2029/30,
totalling £390,560. One scheme (Council Offices Fire Alarm
Upgrade) totalling £69,760 had been brought forward from
2027/28 to 2025/26 resulting in a capital programme for this
committee of four schemes totalling £320,800.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the future capital programme for this
Committee’s services for onward recommendation to Special
Policy and Finance Committee for the period 2026/27 to 2029/30,
based on the proposals included in the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the future capital programme for their services for the period 2026/27 to 2029/30.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report seeking approval from committee for
the new Procurement Strategy covering the period 2025/26 to
2027/28.
 
A review of the Procurement Strategy had been
undertaken following expiry of the previously approved strategy
document. The document covered the same themes as the National
Procurement Strategy for Local Government.
 
No major changes had been made to the
principles contained within the strategy however details of minor
changes were included in the report.
 
The reviewed Procurement Strategy was appended
to the report with the proposed amendments shown in tracked
changes.
 
***RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Recommended to Council the new
Procurement Strategy 2025/26 to 2027/28 as attached to the
report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to recommend the approval of a new Procurement Strategy for the period 2025/26 to 2027/28.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report for Committee to consider the
Council’s Local Council Tax Support (LCTS) Scheme for 2024/25
and submit to Full Council for approval by 11 March 2026.
 
The report noted that the LCTS scheme had
replaced Council Tax Benefit in 2013/14 and was now paid as a
discount against an individual’s council tax bill rather than
a benefit. The Government had replaced the subsidy with a grant
payable to Councils for the cost of LCTS, however they had reduced
the amount from 100% to 90% and councils had either to absorb the
reduction or meet it from reductions in council tax support or
elsewhere from within the council tax system. The Council’s
scheme was broadly similar to the old Council Tax Benefits scheme
but with a 12% reduction in entitlement for claimants of working
age. Following a consultation exercise in 2021, a decision was
taken to remove the 12% reduction in support, which had resulted in
increased LCTS for approximately 1200 households, 600 of which paid
no Council Tax in 2022/23.
 
As part of the budget setting process,
Committee were asked to consider adoption of the Local Council Tax
Support Scheme for determination at the meeting of the Full Council
3 March 2026. No significant changes to the existing scheme were
proposed except for those that would keep it in line with the
Housing Benefit Scheme and increase applicable amounts and
premiums.
 
***RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Recommended the approval of the
Council’s Local Council Tax Support Scheme for 2026/27 to
Full Council.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to recommend the approval of the Council's Local Council Tax Support Scheme for 2026/27.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report seeking Committee approval of the
updated Revenues Discretionary Discount/Relief policy.
 
Local Authorities had the power to grant
discretionary awards to offset council tax and business rates
liabilities, on the basis that qualifying criteria, both national
and local, were met.
 
The revised policy did not make any
significant changes to the existing policy other than incorporating
the business rates measures announced by the government in the
Autum Statement on 26 November 2025, namely:
 

·      
Retail, Hospitality and Leisure (RHL) Relief would cease on 31
March 2026. Going forward, businesses that qualified for the relief
would generally benefit from the new lower RHL multiplier, which in
2026/2027 will be 5p lower than the standard multiplier. Where rate
increases were substantial there will also be transitional
relief.
 

·      
The Supporting Small Business Scheme had been updated to include
changes arising from the 2026 business rates revaluation.
 

·      
The Support for Local Newspapers Scheme ended on 31 March 2025 and
so was no longer referred to within the policy.
 
The full revised Revenues Discretionary
Discount/Relief Policy was included with tracked changes for
Committee’s consideration.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the Revenues Discretionary
Discount/Relief Policy for 2026/27 at appendix 1 of the report.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to approve the updated Revenues Discretionary Discount/Relief policy for 2026/27.

content:
The Director of Resources and Deputy Chief
Executive submitted a report for Committee to agree an updated
Discretionary Housing Payments (DHP) Policy.
 
DHP’s were administered by the benefits
section on behalf of the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) and
provided financial assistance (outside of the Housing Benefits and
Universal Credit Regulations) to help eligible residents meet their
housing costs.
 
From April 2026, DHPs in England would cease
to be delivered under the Discretionary Financial Assistance
Regulations (2001) and the Discretionary Housing Payments (Grants)
Order (2001) and this legislation would be revoked in England.
Going forward, DHPs would be incorporated into the Crisis
Resilience Fund, a fund which would essentially bring together DHPs
and the Household Support Fund. Eligibility, policy objectives,
funding amounts (including admin costs) and recipients remained the
same as those for DHPs in the financial year ending March 2026.
However, Local authorities would be expected to plan for full
integration from April 2028. The DWP would work with authorities
and IT software suppliers to implement changes to support
integration.
 
Committee had previously approved the policy
January 2025. Under the Crisis Resilience Fund, the DHP element
would be retitled ‘Housing Payment’, therefore the
policy had been renamed to reflect this.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved that the Housing
Payment Policy (formerly Discretionary Housing Payment Policy) for
2026/2027 should remain unchanged from that agreed in
2025/2026.
topline: The Policy and Finance Committee has decided to keep the Housing Payment Policy unchanged for the upcoming year, incorporating DHPs into the Crisis Resilience Fund.

content:

Planning submitted a report updating Committee on the UKSPF fund
and the REPF fund and to seek approval for a further scheme.
 
The report provided a list of all previously
approved schemes which resulted in unallocated UKSPF funding
totalling £8,714, and an over allocation of REPF funding
totalling £4,059.
 
The Council had previously been informed of
the requirement for all funding to be spent by the end of March
2026, however the deadline had now been extended to 30 September

identified by the end of March 2026 to ensure the allocation was
spent and because several schemes had a grant agreement in place

An EOI into the Ribble Valley Shared
Prosperity and Jubilee fund had been received from The Friends of

the heritage asset. The working group had considered the request at
their meeting on 9January 2026 and felt the scheme did not meet the
criteria for the Ribble Valley Shared Prosperity and Jubilee Fund
however recommended the scheme for approval under the UKSPF,
utilising the remaining £8714 of funding.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approved the recommendation of the Shared
Prosperity and Jubilee Fund Working Group to provide a UKSPF grant
of £8,714 to the Friends of Kirk Mill to undertake a
feasibility study of the Mill and adjacent pond.
 
Councillor S Hore returned to the meeting and
resumed as Chairman.
topline: The Policy and Finance committee has decided to approve a UKSPF grant of £8,714 to the Friends of Kirk Mill for a feasibility study.

content:

content:
The Chief Executive submitted a
report seeking for Committee to review the market stall
rental statistics for July, August and September 2025 and to agree the proposal to
reduce stall rental fees, as part of a three month campaign, in an
attempt to attract new traders and retain current traders.
 
Clitheroe Market
has benefited from over £200,000 of improvements, creating a
more attractive space that has been positively received, yet the
majority of the bullring casual stalls continue to remain empty.
Despite extensive efforts—including redevelopment, new
branding, social media promotion, collaboration with other markets,
an online booking system, and free stall events—the lack of
traders persists, raising concerns from Councillors, traders, and
the public that the market may decline without more radical
action.
 
It was proposed
that the Council halve current stall fees and offer traders a
second stall at an additional reduced rate on Tuesdays and
Saturdays, removing the little?used third?stall discount. This
would form part of a three?month trial campaign, after which prices
could be reviewed.
 
Members expressed
support for this proposal on a short?term basis, and discussions
were held regarding the marketing of the campaign.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 

1.         Agree
the new stall rental fees (as outlined in paragraph 4.3 of the
report) as part of a 3-month campaign in an attempt to attract new
traders onto the market. The campaign will be held over March,
April and May 2026
 

2.         Subject
to the three-month campaign being agreed; in June 2026, grant
permission for the Head of Environmental Health to extend the
campaign if it proves to be successful.
topline: The Committee has decided to approve a proposal to reduce stall rental fees at Clitheroe Market in an attempt to attract new traders and retain current traders.

content:
The Director of Economic Development and

approval to the draft Health and

Members were

Details were

The Committee

RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Adopt the Health
