charges was co-ordinated by Financial Services, working together
with Heads of Service and budget holders. 
 
It was noted that
if Committee agreed with the proposed fees and charges for
implementation from 1 April 2026 then this Committee would meet the
2.5% target for the financial year 2026/27.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the 2026/27

topline: The Planning and Development Committee has decided to increase fees and charges for services starting April 2026

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report updating Committee on an expected delay
in the delivery of food waste vehicles.
 
Whilst the
collection of food waste from all households will become a
statutory requirement in April 2026, many Councils have
experienced difficulty in procuring the
specific vehicles necessary in time for the start date. The delay
to this council’s delivery was due to circumstances out of
its control following a robust procurement process.
 
The options
available to address the issues were outlined to Members along with
the costs and implications to the Council.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
1.   
Approve the commencement of food waste collections in October 2026
once the Council’s newly procured vehicles have been
delivered.

 
2.   
Revisit this decision in January 2026 if the funding settlement
provides sufficient funds to cover the cost of an earlier
implementation and hire vehicles can be sourced.
topline: The Community Services department has decided to delay the start date of food waste collections to October 2026 due to a delay in the delivery of necessary vehicles.

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report seeking Committee support in recommending
to Policy and Finance Committee approval to bring forward the
capital budget for the refurbishment of the Chatburn Public Toilets
from 2026/27 to this financial year 2025-2026.
 
The request was
being made due to the deterioration in condition of the toilets at
Chatburn.  It was noted that if the
refurbishment was delayed, the current issues would get worse and
result in closing of the toilets.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
1.    
Approve the proposal to undertake the works on Chatburn public
conveniences in the 2025/26 financial year, rather than in 2026/27
as planned.

 
2.    
Request that Policy and Finance Committee approve the bringing
forward in the capital programme of £11,000 from the
Edisford, Bolton-By-Bowland and
Chatburn public conveniences capital scheme in 2026/27 to this
financial year, 2025-2026, to refurbish the Chatburn toilets.
topline: The Director of Community Services has decided to bring forward the refurbishment of Chatburn Public Toilets to prevent their closure due to deteriorating conditions.

content:
Councillor T Austin was granted
permission to speak on this item.
 
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report presenting a proposal to source
additional support for the development of three 3G pitches.
 
Alongside the
£1.45m allocated within the capital budget for a new 3G pitch
at Longridge, the Council received an offer of potential funding
from the Football Foundation to help provide two additional 3G
pitches in the Ribble Valley. 
 
Work has commenced
on the development of the funding bid which will lead to a planning
application in the New Year and a final submission to the Football
Foundation Board for their consideration.  Members were advised that the work required to
develop the funding bid would be significant and internal resources
would be stretched.  As such, it was
proposed that external consultants would be required to assist
officers in completing the necessary work within the timeframe.
 
If funding bids are
submitted successfully, the Football Foundation will fund
approximately 70% of the consultancy costs and the remainder will
be applied to capital project.  If bids
are not submitted for any reason the consultancy costs will most
likely lie with the Council.  The
maximum amount for consultancy costs for all 3 pitches should not
exceed £30k.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the
procurement of external consultants to support the bidding process
to the Football Foundation and present the financial feasibility of
each of the sites, and delegate the appointment of such consultants
and the agreement of any required agreements to the Director of
Community Services in consultation with the Chair of Community
Committee.
topline: The Council has decided to procure external consultants to support the bidding process for the development of three 3G pitches in the Ribble Valley.

content:
The Director of
Resources and Deputy Chief Executive submitted a report seeking
member approval on proposals to increase this Committee’s
fees and charges with effect from 1 April 2026.
 
The proposals were
the first stage in the review of the Committee’s budget for
the forthcoming 2026/27 financial year. Service committees were
asked at this time of year to review their fees and charges
in order to achieve an overall increase
in budgeted income of 2.5%, as assumed in the Council’s
Budget Forecast.
 
The proposed list
of fees and charges for this Committee’s services for
implementation from 1 April 2026 were attached to the report. The
proposed fees and charges were based on a review undertaken by
Financial Services, Heads of Service and budget holders. If Members
agreed to the proposed fees and charges for implementation from 1
April 2026 then budgeted income for this Committee’s fees and
charges would increase in 2026/27 by 2.67%.
 
It was noted that a
small number of the proposed fees and charges for 2026/27 had been
set on a different basis to the guidance of a 2.5%
increase.  In addition, some new fees
had been introduced, some fees had been removed and discount
arrangements for some fees had been amended. These were all
highlighted within the report.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Approve the 2026/27
fees and charges proposed for this Committee in Annex 1 of the
report, for implementation from 1 April 2026.
topline: The Community Services Committee has decided to approve an increase in fees and charges for services starting from 1 April 2026.

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report:
 
-       
updating Committee on the consultation and emerging design for
Castle Grounds in Clitheroe.
-       
seeking agreement from Committee to procure the proposed necessary
public realm works in the Castle Grounds to allow a start on site
in April 2026.
-       
seeking agreement to progress the installation of an outdoor gym
funded by existing ringfenced Section 106 monies and to seek
approval to add this project to the capital programme.
 
A total of
£1.79 million had allocated for Castle Grounds refurbishment
with an additional £588k for Castle Keep
restoration.  It is anticipated that the
Castle Keep work will take place between November 2025 to March
2026.
 
It is proposed that
the Castle Grounds works will be split into two phases:


Phase 1: Outdoor
gym, MUGA refurbishment, park gate restoration.
Phase 2: Pathways,
lighting, seating, signage, and other features (some subject to
further consultation and public engagement).


 
The report detailed
how the Council was undertaking a programme of consultation,
engagement and co-design activities to ensure that partners and
residents can contribute towards the planned improvements to the
castle grounds.
 
Members were also
reminded of the potential to apply for a heritage lottery grant of
up to £250k through its smaller grants scheme. It is
suggested that this would be reconsidered once the relevant
consultation has been completed.
 
As of 4 November
2025, the Skate Park within the Castle grounds will return under
the Council’s control. 
Consultation will take place regarding the possibility of
increasing activities at the park and for relatively minor
improvement works.  A report would be
brought to the next Committee with final proposals.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
1.    
Approve the procurement of Public Realm Works.

 
2.    
Approve the addition of £90,000 to the Castle Grounds capital
scheme in respect of the Installation of the Outdoor Gym, fully
financed through the use of S106 monies,
and refer this to Policy and Finance Committee for approval into
the capital programme.
topline: The Director of Community Services has decided to approve the procurement of public realm works and the addition of an outdoor gym in Castle Grounds in Clitheroe.

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report presenting the recommendations of the
working group in relation to the allocation of grants for Ribble
Valley Christmas Lights 2025.
 
Members were
advised that the budget for the grant was £1,139. Of the
seven applications received for funding, it was recommended that
all receive an amount albeit not the full sum each requested,
because of the large amounts sought by some of the
organisations.
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Endorse the
recommendations of the working group outlined in appendix 1 as
attached to the report.
topline: The Director of Community Services has decided to approve recommendations for the allocation of grants for Ribble Valley Christmas Lights 2025.

content:
The Director of Community Services
submitted a report presenting a proposal to extend the
concession offer at Edisford riverbank
and around the Ribble Valley 3G.
 
The land is
primarily owned by the Council and is currently providing a wide
variety of leisure and recreation facilities.  In addition, there are proposals for further
development of the area. 
 
It is expected that
there would be high demand for refreshments from especially around
the existing 3G pitch area and currently options are being
considered similar to the ice cream concession on the riverbank
 
RESOLVED THAT COMMITTEE:
 
Delegate authority
to the Director of Community Services to implement trial
concessionary offers for the Edisford
3G pitch site and carry out preliminary works to evaluate the
demand for and feasibility of long term concessionary offers and
the potential build of a new permanent structure at the
Edisford River bank site.
topline: The Director of Community Services has decided to extend concession offers at Edisford riverbank and around the Ribble Valley 3G to meet high demand for refreshments.
